as an advance and the monthly Statement of expenditure (SOEs) are monitored by Computerized
Fund Management System (CPFMS). Before the next instalment is released, the previous SOEs is
settled. This process helps in lowering the outstanding amounts with the NGOs.
State AIDS Control Societies (SACS) have already initiated the above steps to keep a tab
on the expenditure of NGOs and thereby decrease the outstanding amounts with the NGOs without
compromising the field implementation. After the statutory audits, SACS recover the unspent
balance amount from NGOs/CBOs and those NGOs not complying with necessary legal actions are

17
taken by involving the district collector or Commissioner. Out of the total outstanding from NGOs
amounting to Rs. 352.7 lakhs in 27 States, an amount of Rs. 221.5 lakhs has been recovered which
is 63 per cent. NGOs in 14 States have a balance of Rs. 131.08 lakhs still to be recovered. District
administration has been requested to expedite the recovery process. Legal actions have also been
initiated against the NGOs who have not responded to the notice. Legal actions have been initiated
for NGOs in 8 States.
VII. PERSONS TO BE COUNSELLED AND TESTED AT ICTCS (TARGET OF 220 LAKH
PER YEAR)
Recommendation/Observation
2.10 The Committee finds that these are fleeting statements based on assumptions. Street
children for example are sexually active at a very young age. New studies also establish that
assumptions that young people below 15 years are not sexually active are not accurate.
Interventions for young people are necessary to address the risk of STDs, HIV and Hepatitis and
the Committee recommends that the Department make appropriate provision for capturing this risk
group. Another scenario was presented before the officials during oral evidence-a long-haul truck
driver/migrant labour (the two highest risk – groups) contracting infection from a sex-worker and
passing it on to his wife back in the village-chances of the wife thus getting infected and becoming
pregnant and being captured as a new case? The Committee for want of a satisfactory answer
recommends that the Department take a very serious view of this critical gap in data generation
as it feels that given the poor accessibility to health care in rural areas the chances of such cases
being captured in data collection would be truly grim. The Committee feels that citing international
norms and a one-size-fits-all kind of approach is neither adequate nor acceptable while capturing
data in a truly diverse country like India. The Department must come up with more innovative
solutions after consulting the various stakeholders so that a more realistic picture is available for
dealing with the HIV menace. The examples quoted are only illustrative and not exhaustive. The
Committee would like to be kept apprised of the initiatives undertaken by the Department in this
regard. (Para 7.3) (a)
Action Taken
The mathematical models of Estimation Projection Package (EPP)/Spectrum used for HIV
Estimation are developed by WHO/UNAIDS Global Reference Group and are adopted in all
countries across the world. The models are developed based on the best available evidence globally
that inform the assumptions in estimating infections in different age groups. Based on the review
of the available evidence on infections among children below 15 years age, the model works on
the assumption that all the HIV infections in children are resulting from Mother to Child
Transmission. Adequate and valid evidence is not available currently that establishes other routes
of transmission among children. Efforts will be made to generate the required information to inform
assumptions in modeling pertaining to the transmission of HIV among children.
In order to capture the effect of migration on HIV transmission in rural areas, sentinel
sites under HIV Sentinel Surveillance are being set up at primary health centres in rural areas in
heavy out-migration districts. This ensures that the pregnant women from these villages are
captured in the data collection efforts to monitor the HIV epidemic. However, poor utilization of
public health settings in rural areas is still a limitation to HIV Sentinel Surveillance activities.
Besides surveillance, special in-depth studies are also being conducted to study the dynamics of
HIV transmission due to migration and these studies also inform the programme about the ways
to control it.

18
Recommendation/Observation
2.11 The Committee observes that HIV , Hepatitis B, Hepatitis C share common modes of
transmission. The Committee recommends that the technical feasibility of ICTC centres expansion
to test and counsel for hepatitis in a p hased manner should be undertaken immediately. This is
important as many experts feel that there is a significant but under recognized hepatitis-associated
disease burden in this country. Despite that India does not have a Hepatitis disease registry, or
information on the diseases burden. For example, a Professor & Head of Gastroenterology at
AIIMS, has stated that studies reported from various parts of India estimate that about 20 million
Indians are Hepatitis B carriers and about 8 to 10 million may have silent Hepatitis C virus
infection. These individuals do not know that they have these infections and not only are at risk
of transmitting this disease but also cannot access early treatment preventing late stage liver
cirrhosis and liver cancer. (Para 7.3 (b))
Action Taken
The diagnosis and management of Hepatitis B and Hepatitis C to people attending the
hospitals is the mandate of the general health system, as these facilities are provided in the existing
health care delivery system. Thus, Department of AIDS Control may not duplicate efforts to
provide such facilities in the set up of National AIDS Control Programme as such facilities are in
the large number of cases, located in the same institution. Whenever a PLHIV attends an ART
centre and is found to be co-infected with Hepatitis B and Hepatitis C, he/she is referred to the
general health system for confirmatory diagnosis and management of Hepatitis B and Hepatitis C.
VIII. ANTIRETROVIRAL TREATMENT (ART) CENTRES
Recommendation/Observation
2.12 The Committee feels that it would be in the fitness of things to upgrade the link centres
to ART centres in order to increase the number of patients who can avail treatment as well as
procure drugs near their residence which would go a long way in decreasing the staggering figures
of patients who cannot avail treatment due to inaccessibility of the existing ART centres in the
country. (Para 8.6)
Action Taken
As has been pointed out by the Committee in para 8.5, it is understood that HIV virus is
prone to drug resistance. As ART is a specialised treatment, scale up of facilities to provide ART
is done with caution. NACP stresses proper counselling of patients to ensure complete adherence
to treatment, to prevent drug resistance. As per scheme of Link ART Centres, these centres are
upgraded to ART centres once they have a critical mass of patients for treatment at the centre.
They require adequate infrastructure and other facilities to undertake this specialised care in the
interest of the patients.

19
CHAPTER-III
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS IN RESPECT OF WHICH REPLIES
OF THE GOVERNMENT HA VE NOT BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE COMMITTEE
II. BUDGETARY ALLOCATION
Recommendation/Observation
3.1 The Committee notes that with focused intervention of NACO, there is a considerable
decline in unspent balances available with the societies. The Committee would, however, like to
point out that availability of unspent balances with some SACS like Andhra Pradesh SACS (17.59
crore), Karnataka SACS (Rs. 21.09 crore), Madhya Pradesh SACS (Rs. 15.02 crore) and Tamil
Nadu SACS (Rs. 14.68 crore) is still quite high. The Committee, therefore, recommends to the
Department to introduce stricter monitoring mechanism and financial discipline so that funds do not
get accumulated and remain unutilized. The Committee also impresses upon the Department to
ensure fixing of responsibility to ensure proper accountability in utilization of funds. (Para 2.10)
Action Taken
3.2 Recommendations of the Committee are noted for compliance. It is always the endeavor of
the Department to keep balances with the SACS to the minimum. With respect to unspent balance
available with Andhra Pradesh SACS, Karnataka SACS, Madhya Pradesh SACS and Tamil Nadu
SACS, it is submitted that other than Madhya Pradesh the other three states exhibit high prevalence
of HIV/AIDS and have a high concentration of programme activities. Their annual budgets are
correspondingly large. The final availability of unspent balances at the end of the financial year
2011-12 for these SACS are Andhra Pradesh (Rs.7.24crore), Karnataka (Rs.14.83 crore), Madhya
Pradesh (Rs.16.09 crore) and Tamil Nadu (Rs.6.14 crore). While all efforts are made to ensure that
SACS do not have idle unspent balances, it must also be appreciated that there is a necessity to
have funds available with SACS at all times as working capital to meet program expenditure and
avoid any hiccup in programme implementation due to a fund flow problem.
Continuous monitoring has ensured that though opening cash balance as on 1.4.2011 was
Rs. 206.32 crore, closing balance as on 31.3.2012 was Rs. 145.37 crore which represents a
significant improvement.
Further Recommendation
3.3 The Committee is concerned that a balance of Rs.147.37 crore remaining as unspent
balance is still a very substantial amount and warrants constant efforts on the part of the
Government to wipe out the same. The Committee, therefore, recommends to the
Department to devise innovative ways to reduce the balance to the minimum and ensure
financial prudence and propriety.
V. SETTING UP OF NEW DISTRICT LEVEL BLOOD BANKS
Recommendation/Observation
3.2 The Committee notes that against the target of setting up of 39 Blood banks during the
19

20
Eleventh Plan, only 25 Blood Banks could be set up. When enquired about the reasons for
non-completion of 14 blood banks, the Department has stated that this was on account of various
factors like non-completion of infrastructure, in-adequate man-power, lack of equipments and non-
acquisition of license etc. But the Committee feels that the reasons illustrated by the Department
are frivolous. It appears that the Department has not made sincere efforts to achieve the physical
targets. The Committee desires that the Department should make concerted efforts to complete the
processes as mentioned above by the December, 2012, so that the time line set by NACP-III is
adhered to . (Para 5.3)
Action Taken
3.5 As identified in NACP III the Blood Safety component of DAC was committed to facilitate
setting up of District Level Blood Banks at the District Hospitals in 39 newly created districts of
which 25 have been established. The 39 districts with no blood bank were identified in the States
of Bihar, U.P, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Kerala, Karnataka, Mizoram, and Uttarakhand.
As per the norms the State needs to provide land, infrastructure, equipments and manpower
before support of laboratory technician, some equipment support and consumables are provided
under this scheme.
At present 25 DLBBs have been set up. Of the remaining 14 cases, in 6 districts
construction of the building for blood banks is complete and steps are being taken to meet the
requirements for a license.
In 8 other districts, blood bank buildings are under construction. Instructions have been
issued by NACO to the respective SACS to set up a Blood Storage Centre in these districts till
the new blood banks become operational.
In the States where infrastructure has still not been provided the target cannot be attained
till December 2012. However in the remaining sites where basic infrastructure is available all efforts
will be made to have the blood banks functional.
Further Recommendation
3.6 The Committee is dismayed to observe the snail’s pace of progress for setting up the
remaining 14 District Level Blood Banks (DLBBs), out of 39 DLBBs under Phase-III of
NACO. Factual position as given by the Department clearly indicates that majority of the
State Governments have failed to fulfill their commitments of providing infrastructure. The
Committee is of the firm opinion that the difficulties as pointed out by the Department are
not insurmountable and can be taken care of if the matter is pursued vigorously with the
State Governments concerned at the highest level. The Committee, therefore, would like to
impress upon the Department to play a proactive role by taking up the matter with the
concerned State Governments, if need be, at the highest level, and inform the Committee
of the efforts made in this regard and the outcome thereof.
Recommendation/Observation
3.7 The Committee is surprised that in spite of the Committee’s recommendation made in its
42
nd Report on Demands for Grants (2010-11), the Department has moved at a snail’s pace which
is evident from the fact that it has managed only to get the land allotted in November 2011 for
the four metro blood banks. The Committee is dismayed by the callousness on the part of the
Department to disregard its recommendation to have a targeted approach in making the four metro
blood banks functional at the earliest. The Committee expresses its displeasure at this sorry state

21
of affairs and recommends that the Secretary of the Department should take personal interest to
ensure completion of the four Metro Blood Banks at the earliest. (Para 5.7)
Action Taken
3.8 • The Proposal for Setting up of Metro Blood Banks was one of the approved activities
under NACP- Phase III.
• As building and manpower were not part of the proposal, a revised proposal was
submitted to EFC and then to Cabinet for approval.
• Under the scheme, it is envisaged to get the requisite land free of cost by respective
State Governments. However, being all the 4 sites in metro-cities, it was difficult to get
requisite piece of land of this size, that too, in vicinity of medical college hospital.
• The land transfer has been done for sites at Kolkata, Mumbai & Chennai. While for
Delhi site, the same is still pending.
• The DPR 2 for the sites at Chennai, Mumbai and Kolkata was approved by the Steering
Committee on 20.12.2011.
• Revised EFC Memo was circulated on 29.2.2012 and has since been redrafted in view
of revised format issued by Ministry of Finance and due to time and cost overrun a
Standing Committee report has to be enclosed with the Revised Cost Estimate.
• Since the examination of the Department by this august Committee, a Standing
Committee on Time & Cost Overrun, chaired by Secretary, DAC has been constituted.
This committee had two meetings and has submitted its findings on 7.6.2012. The
minutes of the same are under circulation. They will be annexed with the draft RCE for
circulation shortly.
• All efforts are being made by the Department to accelerate the establishment and
functioning of these Metro Blood Banks which will be initiated after all approvals are
obtained.
Further Recommendation
3.5 The Committee is constrained to observe that the Project concerning setting up of
the Metro Blood Banks has been plagued by delays due to faulty planning which is evident
from the fact that building and manpower were not part of the original proposal which
necessitated submission of a revised proposal first to EFC and then to Cabinet and thus
resulted in time and cost overruns. More than two and a half years have passed since the
Committee made recommendations in this regard in its 42nd Report presented to
Parliament on the 28th April, 2010, but the execution of the project still remains a far cry.
The Committee, therefore, urges upon the Department to review the strategies adopted so
far in the implementation of the Project and incorporate necessary modifications in the
same with a view to expedite the project at the earliest.
VII. PERSONS TO BE COUNSELED AND TESTED AT ICTCs (TARGETS OF 220 LAKH
PER YEAR)
Recommendation/Observation
3.10 As per information submitted by the Department, it has set an overall target of 220 lakh

22
people per year (including pregnant women) to be counselled and tested in ICTCs at the end of
NACP III i.e. March, 2012. However, a plain reading of the figures furnished by the Department
reveals that the Department has not been able to achieve its scaled down targets. Further, as per
information furnished by the Department, total approved number of posts of counsellors in ICTCs
is 4992 whereas the actual strength is 4774. Similarly the sanctioned strength of the post of lab
technicians in ICTCs is 4702 whereas the actual strength is 4352. The Committee expresses
displeasure that the Department has not been able to fulfill even its scaled down targets. However,
the Committee supports any endeavour by means of which the Department would be able to
achieve the targets fixed by it. If need be, it would support the Department to seek additional funds
from the Finance Ministry/Planning Commission so as to augment the manpower as well as number
of stand-alone ICTCs with the rider that the Department makes serious efforts to achieve its yearly
targets. (Para 7.2)
Action Taken
3.11 The Department has made efforts to scale up counseling and testing services by
collaborating with NRHM to establish Facility Integrated Counseling and Testing Centres. Workload
of ICTC is continuously reviewed to ensure optimal utilization of available human resource.
The vacancies among counselors and laboratory technicians has been a constant challenge
for the Department due to
(i) inability of some States like Odisha to fill up the vacancies due to court cases and
other administrative issues
(ii) attrition of staff at field level
(iii) overall shortage of qualified laboratory technicians in the States
To address this challenge, wherever there is a vacancy, the department ensured continuity
of counseling and testing services by training the general health system laboratory technician and
utilizing their services.
Further Recommendation
3.12 The Committee is not satisfied with the reply of the Department. The Committee
feels that if the court cases had been pursued vigorously, pronouncement of verdicts could
have been expedited. As regards resolving administrative issues and dealing with attrition
of staff at field level, the Committee is of the firm view that these issues could have been
easily taken care of by streamlining the decision-making process and offering adequate
incentives. The Committee, therefore, would like the Department to show vision in dealing
with such issues and advise the State Governments accordingly, instead of devoting its
energies to quick-fix solutions.
IX. NEW INITIATIVES
(i) SETTING UP OF NATIONAL BLOOD TRANSFUSION AUTHORITY (NBTA)
Recommendation/Observation
3.13 The Committee expresses its dismay over the fact that the Department of Expenditure has
not sent its comments so far. Though the original timeline for starting NBTA was April, 2010, there
is still no ray of hope of its being set up in near future. The Committee condemns such
procrastinating attitude of the government. The Committee impress upon the Department that in
order to ensure setting up of a National Blood Transfusion Authority, it is imperative that immediate

23
steps should be taken to remove the legal infirmities raised by the Ministry of Finance along with
seeking replies from respective Departments without further delay in view of the fact that the
scheme which was to take wings in the Eleventh Plan is yet to take off. (Para 9.2)
Action Taken
Status Note on Establishment of National Blood Transfusion Authority (NBTA)
3.14 • The Proposal for Setting up of NBTA was one of the approved activities under NACP-
Phase III.
• A vision document on NBTA was prepared in 2008 which was reviewed during a
meeting of experts.
• The proposed budget allocation for NBTA was 39.55 crores for 2 years under NACPIII.
• A draft Cabinet note was prepared and sent to various departments such as Dept. of
Expenditure and Economic Affairs, under Ministry of Finance, Dept of Health and
Planning Commission for comments in September 2009
The Ministry of Finance has not supported the proposal and the detailed observations are
as given below:
1. The intent of NBTA and SBTAs, as clarified in the responses of the revised proposal
is facilitation of the regularity functions of the DCI. These functions can be done
through the existing set up of NBTC and SBTCs which were set up for the purpose.
If necessary, these existing entities could be further strengthened.
2. It has been indicated that State Governments spend Rs. 700 Crore on blood banks
annually and the intent is that these funds would be provided to NBTA to enable it
manage these blood banks through the respective SBTAs. Prima facie, it is not clear
why the State Governments would provide these funds to NBTA without a specific legal
provision, or whether alternate/additional central funding is being conceived here. It is
difficult to support the present formulation without a clear understanding of the fund
requirement and its source in the present case.
3. What appears to have been proposed is taking over regulation and administration of
blood banks (including financial administration) by NBTA through SBTAs. Prima facie,
it does not appear to be feasible without a clear legal mandate in this regard.
4. The fund requirement (over 2010-12) for establishing the NBTA and SBTAs has been
reduced and it has been stated that these funds would be made available out of
NACPIII. Even as the source of funding of the new proposed entities has been clarified
there remains a requirement of appraisal of expenditure proposals at the appropriate
forum before considering their approval.
In view of the above, the matter was not pursued further.
Further Recommendation
3.16 While looking into the reasons for non-approval of the proposal, the Committee finds
that the basic premise for non-approval of the same is the legal infirmities existing in the
present scheme and the requirement of appraisal of the expenditure proposals at the
appropriate forum before considering their approval. The Committee, therefore, impresses
upon the Department to have a relook at the scheme based on Finance Ministry’s detailed
observations and try to remove the infirmities and submit the same again for reconsideration
and approval.

24
(ii) SETTING UP OF PLASMA FRACTIONATION CENTRE (PFC)
Recommendation/Observation
3.17 The Committee is disappointed by the snail’s pace to set up Plasma Fractionation Centre
which is still bogged down in bureaucratic red-tapism even though the Eleventh Five Year Plan has
come to an end. The Committee, therefore, impresses upon the Department to make all out efforts
for setting up of Plasma Fractionation Centre without any further delay. (Para 9.4)
Action Taken
• The Proposal for Setting up of Plasma Fractionation Centre was one of the approved
activities under NACP-Phase III.
• The Centre will have the capacity to fractionate 1.5 lakh litres of plasma per annum
collected from all NACO supported blood banks in the country
• The direct benefit of implementation of this project is to ensure access of plasma
derivatives to needy patients at affordable costs. This will also reduce our dependence
on imported products saving the foreign exchange.
• As building and manpower were not part of the proposal, a supplementary proposal was
submitted for approval.
• The total outlay for the scheme is Rs. 250 crores.
Current Status
• Tamil Nadu Government has provided the land for establishing the PFC at New Avadi
Road, Anna Nagar, Chennai measuring approximately 1.5 acres.
Issues of Concern
EOI for the Project Management Consultant selection was published in May, 2010. During
July, 2009 to January, 2011 the blood safety work was placed at Ministry of Health and Family
Welfare as per decision of Hon’ble HFM which has been transferred to Department of AIDS
Control since January, 2011. In this period NACO convened national and international consultations
to arrive at the technology to be used for the PFC plant. As the proposal was prepared with costing
of 2007-08 it is likely that the estimated cost will be escalated which may require a fresh EFC
approval.
Departmental Efforts to remove bottlenecks
A meeting of the expert group was held on 4 th February, 2011 which short listed 5
companies amongst the 14 EOIs received as Project Management Consultant (PMC).
Request for Proposal (RFP) was prepared for onward communication to the selected
companies. No company was found to be suitable for the same and the whole process is being
reworked.
As the country has no expertise in the area of plasma fractionation the project has been
delayed. Further, cartelization of the technology providers in this area is causing concern in
identifying the appropriate technical resources. Further, the cost estimation will be revised as there
has been an escalation in the price since 2007-08.

25
Further Recommendation
3.19 The Committee is dismayed at the manner in which setting up of a Plasma
Fractionation Centre is still entangled in paper work. It shows the lackadaisical approach
of the Department for setting up Plasma Fractionation Centre. Though, the reply of the
Department indicates the progress made so far, the reasons for the delay are not justified.
In the opinion of the Committee, this is a case of poor planning and implementation
strategy on the part of the Department. The Committee, therefore, recommends to the
Department to revisit its strategy and set out necessary time-bound corrective measures to
achieve the target at the earliest.
XVI. HIV/AIDS Bill
Recommendation/Observation
3.20 The Committee expresses its displeasure on inordinate delay in bringing about HIV/AIDS Bill
even though six years have lapsed since it was first drafted in 2006. The reasons given by the
Department are not acceptable and frivolous and clearly indicate the manner in which it continues
to sideline this crucial law that is aimed at not only protecting the rights of people living with HIV
and marginalized population but also to protect public health. The cases of discrimination in
healthcare, education and within their families have not gone down and in fact continue to endanger
the lives of millions of HIV+, while the Department delays action. The Committee, therefore,
recommends that the Department should take urgent measures to speed up the process for
introduction of the bill as soon as possible, keeping in view the nature of the diseases. (Para 14.4)
Action Taken
3.21 The recommendation of the Committee has been noted. As indicated earlier, the draft of the
Bill was recast and referred to Ministry of Law and Justice in September, 2011 and again in
December, 2011 for vetting. Thereafter, a note along with the draft of the Bill was prepared which
was circulated to various Ministries/Departments in March, 2012, for their comments. The
comments of most of the Ministries/Departments have been received which are being examined.
Comments of few are awaited. They have been reminded to expedite their comments. The
Department has been taking all measure to speed up the process for completion of various
requirements before introduction of the Bill in the Parliament.
Further Recommendation
3.22 The Committee understands that the proposed HIV/AIDS Bill requires detailed
analysis before being introduced in the Parliament. At the same time the Committee
expects that the Department could have been more proactive in taking the Bill to its logical
conclusion. The Committee, therefore, urges upon the Department to take concrete steps
to ensure that the Bill is introduced at the earliest.

CHAPTER-I
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS IN RESPECT OF WHICH REPLIES
OF THE GOVERNMENT HAVE BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE COMMITTEE
BUDGETARY ALLOCATION
Recommendation/Observation
1.1 The Committee notes that in-principle approval of the Planning Commission has already
been obtained for most of the Schemes which could not take off during the Eleventh Plan due
to lack of necessary approvals. The Schemes or sub-components of the Schemes, which have
received Planning Commission’s in-principle approval, include Promotion and Guidance on
Research Governance Issues, Inter-sectoral Coordination in Medical, Biomedical and Health
Research, Advanced Training in Research in Medicine and Health, Matters relating to
Epidemics, Natural Calamities and Development of Tools; Coordination in the field of Health
Research with Governments, Organisations and Institutes; Matters relating to Scientific
Societies and Associations; Charitable and Religious Endowments in Medicine and Health
Research areas etc. The Committee takes note of the submission of the Department of Health
Research that the allocated funds for the year 2012-13 would be able to meet only part of the
cost of the new activities and this resource crunch from the beginning would seriously affect
the goals of Department, especially new activities. The Committee, therefore, views with
serious concern the considerably reduced BE allocation vis-à-vis  projected outlay for 2012-13 .
(Para 2.12)
Action Taken
DHR has planned its schemes as per the projected outlay for the 12th Plan. However, DHR
will initiate its activities within allotted budget for 2012-13 and will request the Finance Division/
Planning Commission to increase the allocation at RE stage. Department will try its best to achieve
the targets depending upon the availability of the funds.
The Department is thankful to the Hon’ble Committee for accepting its submission that the
funds allocated will enable it to only meet a part of the costs of the new activities and for its
concern for the adverse impact this will have on the Department’s goals.
Recommendation/Observations
1.2 Considering the fact that scientific knowledge generated through health and biomedical
research is used to develop drugs, diagnostics, vaccines, and devices that ultimately find place
in the health care delivery systems of the country as also the fact that health research has a
vital role to play in discovery and development of indigenous health products, the Committee
recommends that the allocation for the Department for 2012-13 be suitably enhanced at RE
stage. The Committee would simultaneously recommend that the Department should deploy its
resources in a more efficient manner and ensure optimal utilization of the allocated funds.
(Para 2.13)

The Department is thankful to the Hon’ble Committee for recommending an enhancement
of the allocations made to the Department for 2012-13 at the RE stage.
The Department will like to assure the Hon’ble Committee that it will strive hard to ensure

Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR)
Recommendation/Observation
1.3 The Committee observes that in a resource-constrained country like India judicious
utilization of funds is of paramount importance. Equally important is the fact that the attention
should be focused on health outcomes rather than health outlays. The Committee would, therefore,
like the Department to get all on-going research projects, being funded, wholly or partially with
Government money, evaluated by an independent agency and place the findings in the public
domain. (Para 3.26)
Action Taken
As advised, the Department will formulate the strategies for analysing the research outputs
in terms of health outcomes. Currently the final reports of all the projects are evaluated by ‘external
and independent’ Project Review Committees constituted for different subjects. The Department
will take action to put these findings and opinions of the Expert Committees as well as specific
evaluation of health outcome in public domain as recommended by the Standing Committee.
The Department is thankful to the Hon’ble Committee for endorsing its assessment that the
efforts in the domain of health research should be targeted at health outcomes, and benefits
accruing to the common man through more efficient therapeutics, affordable diagnostics and
products.
The Department will implement the recommendation of the Hon’ble Committee to get the
research activities (intramural/extramural), currently being peer reviewed by non-CMR subject
experts, evaluated by an independent agency and place the findings in the public domain.
Recommendation/Observation

greater clarity, the Committee would like to recommend to the Department to introduce the above
achievements into the public health systems of the country at the earliest opportunity. The
Committee would like to be apprised of the progress made in this direction. (Para 3.28)

For the purpose of the assessment of technology/knowledge advancement into public health
care system, the department has already constituted an advisory group for working out the

and to make recommendations for inclusion of technology/knowledge advancement in public health
system. The progress of the same will be communicated to the Parliamentary Standing Committee
on Health and Family Welfare. The Department is thankful to the Hon’ble Committee for its
appreciation of ICMR’s achievements.
The progress made in regard to the 30 leads being pursued for conversion into diagnostics
etc., is indicated in the Annexure.

The Planning Commission has been apprised of the Hon’ble Committees’ views on the

would require involvement of a number of agencies/organizations. Anticipating this, the Committee
in its 40th Report presented to Parliament on the 28th April 2010, had inter-alia recommended to
the Department to create an institutional coordination mechanism for synergizing the core
competencies of the different research organizations/agencies. In pursuance of the Committee’s

affordable health care available to the poor/marginalized groups/communities. The Committee
observes that in the post Trade-related Intellectual Property Rights (TRIPs) era, development of
indigenous pharma products and medical devices are of momentous importance without which
making affordable healthcare a reality to the marginalized sections of the society would remain
a chimera. The Committee, would therefore, like the Department to sufficiently prioritize research
activities which are oriented towards developing indigenous pharma products and medical
devices . (Para 5.11)

CHAPTER-II
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS WHICH THE COMMITTEE DOES
NOT DESIRE TO PURSUE IN VIEW OF THE GOVERNMENT’S REPLIES
BUDGETARY ALLOCATION
Recommendation/Observation
2.1 The Committee is constrained to observe that there is a huge mismatch to the tune of
Rs. 2379.43 crore between the Eleventh Plan outlay and the Plan allocations made for the
Department of Health Research. The Committee feels that the financial outlay earmarked for the
Eleventh Plan was based more on theoretical anticipation rather than factors like past trends of
expenditure, stages of formulation/implementation of various projects, the status of pre-project
approvals etc. The Committee would, therefore, strongly recommend that all possible measures
should be put in place to exercise greater financial prudence for the purpose of earmarking realistic
outlays for the Twelfth Plan Period. (Para 2.6)
Action Taken
Against the approved plan outlay of Rs.4496.08 crores by the Planning Commission, the
actual allotment of funds to the D/o Health Research amounted to Rs.2116.65 crore and the actual
expenditure was Rs.1933 crores. It would therefore, be observed that utilisation against actual
allocation was 91.30 percent. The minor shortfall was due to the establishment of the department
in the later half of 2007, belated ‘in principle’ approval to the schemes of DHR by the Planning
Commission in December 2010 and non-approval of the two schemes within the Eleventh Plan due
to procedural delays and partial approval of other two schemes by the internal finance division of
the Ministry with their scope reduced to include only the remaining period of Eleventh Plan, that
too only for the last few months of the last year of the Eleventh Plan, i.e. 2011-12.
The Department would follow the financial prudence while drafting its demands for fund
in future. The Twelfth Plan was prepared after detail discussion. The department has taken up the
matter with the Planning Commission for earmarking outlay commensurate with the projects/
schemes of the Department.
Recommendation/Observation
2.2 The Committee understands that the 12th Plan outlay of the Department is yet to be
approved. The Committee observes that the delay in formal approval of the 12th Plan outlay has
a direct bearing on the process of EFC/CCEA approvals of various schemes/programmes of the
Department and their implementation. The Committee observes that the 11th Plan has already
concluded in March, 2012 and the process of approval of the 12th Plan should have been
completed much before so as to obviate procrastination. The Committee, accordingly, recommends
to the Government to quickly complete all the formalities related to planning process and approve
the 12th Plan outlay in right earnest so that the implementation of various schemes/programmes of
the Department is not hampered by lack of approvals. (Para 2.14)

7
Action Taken
DHR has incorporated the recommendations of the Standing Committee while preparing
EFCs of the four schemes for submission to Government. The EECs of the four schemes have
been submitted for appraisal and requisite approvals. The Department has done the ground work
to launch its schemes as soon as the approvals are granted.
The Hon’ble Committee’s concern at the delay in the finalisation of the Departments’ 12th
Plan outlay, and its consequential adverse impact on the schemes/programmes of the Department
has been communicated to the Planning Commission.
Development of Infrastructure for Promotion of Health Research
Recommendation/Observation
2.3 The Committee welcomes the initiatives taken by the Department for establishment of MRUs
and MRHRUs. The Committee observes that while there is clarity about the fact that the
government medical colleges would be given support for development of infrastructure in terms of
establishment of multidisciplinary research units, there is lack of clarity on the policy stance of the
Development about the model ( i.e. government, private or PPP) to be adopted for establishing the
MRHRU. The Committee expects the Department to remove this ambiguity. (Para 4.7)
Action Taken
The Department will like to inform the Hon’ble Committee that in its considered view the
proposed MRHRUs’ are proposed to be set up as a Government activity and not in a PPP mode.
The scheme has been formulated by the Department in two parts provides for (1) establishment
of Multi-Disciplinary Health Research Units (MRUs) in Government Medical Colleges with 100%
financial support by the DHR for period of five years and thereafter, transfer of recurring
expenditure liability to the concerned State Government/Medical Colleges; and (2) establishment of
Model Rural Health Research Unit (MHRUs) to be run as Departmental Units with 100% funding
by the Department of Health Research and the State Governments responsibility will be limited for
providing requisite land.
The MRHRU will drive the research agenda as per local/regional needs so that the
technology is introduced into the States as per their needs on dynamic basis. This aspect has since
been clearly delineated in the proposal for the EFC.
Recommendation/Observation
2.4 The Committee notes that the above initiatives are targeted to bridge the gap in the
availability of infrastructure for research in medical colleges and create infrastructure for transfer
of technology to the beneficiaries in rural areas. From the information furnished by the Department,
the Committee gathers that EFC for this scheme is yet to be approved whereas the Planning
Commission has accorded its in-principle approval to it. For enabling operationalization of the
Scheme at the earliest, the Committee would expect the Department to make vigorous efforts to
get the clearance of EFC at the earliest and obviate further delays. The Committee desires to be
apprised of the steps taken by the Department to get the EFC approval expedited. (Para 4.8)
Action Taken
Department has already started its efforts to get the approval of its scheme in question. The
EFC for the Scheme for Twelfth Plan Period have already been prepared and processed through

8
IFD for circulation amongst the appraisal agencies and obtaining requisite approvals, as per the
prescribed procedure.
Recommendation/Observation
2.5 The Committee apprehends that meagre outlay of Rs. 44 crore would not be sufficient to
meet the requirement of funds under this head, especially in view of the fact that development of
infrastructure is a capital-intensive activity and 60 proposals for establishment of MRUs and
detailed proposals for establishment of MRHRUs from five States have already been received. The
Committee, therefore, recommends that the Planning Commission have a re-look at the allocations
made under the above head and revise it upwardly at RE stage. (Para 4.10)
Action Taken
The Planning Commission has been apprised of the Hon’ble Committee’s concerns about the
adverse effects of the reduced outlay on this capital intensive scheme, and its desire that the outlay
be enhanced at the RE stage.

period, indicating the time line/project implementation schedule. The Department has initiated its

Human Resource Development for Health Research
Recommendation/Observation
2.8 The Committee is supportive of the Programme and observes that without a strong human

Recommendation/Observation
3.10 The Committee observes that the shortfall between the projected demand and the Budget
Estimate for ICMR for 2012-13 is to the tune of Rs. 1183.00 crore, which is massive by any
standards and is certain to have an adverse bearing on the implementation of various intramural and
extramural research projects of ICMR. Given the excellent track-record of ICMR in utilizing the
budgeted funds, the Committee wonders as to what financial yardstick was applied leading to
substantially reduced allocation of funds in BE 2012-13 vis-à-vis the projected demand. In view of
the dynamic international health research environment and the current and future health challenges
of the country, the role of ICMR is very crucial in generating new knowledge in frontier areas of
research on health and related issues and if its projects are allowed to be plagued with under-
funding to such a large extent, it can have very serious repercussions for generation of new
scientific knowledge and undermine the desired outcomes in health sector. The Committee,

CHAPTER-I
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS IN RESPECT OF WHICH REPLIES
OF THE GOVERNMENT HAVE BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE COMMITTEE
I. BUDGETARY PROVISIONS
Recommendations/Observations
1.1 The Department has informed that the expenditure status of the allocated funds under Plan
heads for the Eleventh Plan was as follows:
(Rs. in crore )
Year B E RE Actual Expdt.
2007-08 2985.00 2331.39 2183.83
2008-09 3650.00 3650.00 3008.40
2009-10 4450.00 3825.25 3261.90
2010-11 5560.00 5139.55 4666.04
2011-12 5720.00 4450.00 4101.41
Total – XI Plan 22365.00 19396.19 17221.58
(Para 1.1)
1.2 From a scrutiny of the above Table, the Committee is constrained to observe that there was
substantial and persistent under-utilization of the budgeted funds during the Eleventh Plan. That the
savings occurred under the Plan head underlines the fact that the development activities have been
curtailed. Though the Committee is supportive of the Department’s demand for higher allocation of
funds, it deprecates the Department for failing to optimally utilize its Plan Allocations over the last
five years. The Committee observes that the underutilization of budgeted funds is indicative of slack
monitoring on the part of the Department as well as formulation of the Budget Estimates in a
ritualistic manner without application of proper financial yardsticks. The Committee, accordingly,
impresses upon the Department to pay focused attention to streamlining its monitoring mechanism
and ensure optimal and more efficient deployment and utilization of its financial resources for
smooth execution of its Plan programmes. (Para 1.2)
Action Taken
Noted for compliance.
Recommendations/Observations
1.3 As per the information furnished by the Department the allocation made vis-a-vis actual
expenditure incurred in respect of some of the major Institutions/projects/initiatives of Department
for the last three financial years is as follows: Annexure-I (Para 1.12)
2

3
1.4 From a perusal of the utilization trend of the allocation as given in the Table above, the
Committee infers that the Department has failed to meet broad committed objectives of the Eleventh
Five Year plan. The Committee feels that the Department needs to introspect the reasons for
underutilization of funds practically in all of its major initiatives targeted to be achieved during the
Eleventh Plan period and take appropriate corrective actions accordingly. In addition to dedicated
approach, advance action plans may also be drawn for completion of all the projects in hand within
the targeted timelines. (Para 1.13)
Action Taken
Noted for compliance.
Recommendations/Observations
1.5 The Committee recalls the following recommendations it has made in its 39th Report:–
“The Committee takes note of the fact that the Department has taken measures like for
non-recurring grants, no fresh releases are being authorized unless audited Utilization
Certificate for grant released in the year prior to the last year ( i.e. with a ‘grace period’
of one year) has been received, subject to the condition that the sanction for the earlier
grant does not permit a longer period of utilization. Further, the provisions of the General
Financial Rules, which require that in case of recurring grants, funds for same purpose
beyond 75% of the next year’s provision will not be released unless audited Utilization
Certificate for the grants released in the previous year is received, are being strictly
implemented. Impact of such measures does not seem to be very effective as number of
pending UCs continues to remain very high. Not only this, such a trend also indicates that
schemes are not being implemented as envisaged.”
“The Committee notes that as a further effort to maximize liquidation of UCs, a
communication has been sent by the Secretary (Health) to the Principal Health Secretaries
of all the States. If need be, this exercise needs to be pursued further with higher
authorities.” (Para 1.18)
1.6 The Committee is deeply disturbed that no heed has been paid to the Committee’s above
observations/recommendations, and a large number of UCs are still pending under both the
Centrally Sponsored and Central Sector Schemes. The additional measure taken by the Department
by sending a communication from the Secretary (Health) to the Principal Health Secretaries of all
the States has also been proved to be futile. The Committee, accordingly, recommends that the
Department needs to have a serious introspection of the reasons for pendency of such a large
number of Utilization Certificates and come out with clear and innovative action plans for
liquidation thereof. (Para 1.19)
Action Taken
The Office of CCA has been periodically monitoring the pendency of UCs at the level of
different State Governments, and putting up the status to higher authorities in the Ministry. D.O.
letter has been issued to all the Health Secretaries with details of UCs pending in the States. Many
States like Punjab, Tripura, Goa, Jharkhand, Haryana have already responded with details of the
UCs. A drive to reconcile the pending UCs with Divisions shall be undertaken during this quarter.
A monitoring system has also been introduced on the website of CCA namely
www.ccahealth@gov.in to monitor the status of UCs.

4
Recommendation/Observation
1.7 The Committee is constrained to note that to a pointed query to the Department in this
regard, the Department has either merely stated that the ATN has been submitted to the Audit or
the ATN is under preparation. The Committee rather desires that details of the Action Taken by the
Department on the Audit paras should have been made available to the Committee. The Committee
also takes note of the fact that action on audit paras dating as far back to years 2008, 2009 are
still under preparation stage. The Committee calls for a speedy action on the observations as
contained in audit paras. The Committee would like to be apprised of the action taken in this
regard. (Para 1.21)
Action Taken
The details of ATN on audit paras are at Annexure-II.
As regards speedy action on the submission of ATN on audit paras, following monitoring
system has been put in place to review the status of pending Action Taken Notes:
1. The Standing Audit Committee has been set up under the Chairmanship of Secretary
(Health) with AS&FA, CCA and concerned Joint Secretary as members to review the
pending ATN regularly.
2. ATN Adalats/Workshops with the representatives of audit are held to review the
pending Action Taken Notes/Disputes.
3. Status of pending Action Taken Notes is also reviewed in the Senior Officers’ Meeting
periodically.
4. The Committee of Secretaries is also reviewing the status of pending Action Taken
Notes.
As a result of above reviews, pendency of Action Taken Notes on audit paras has been
greatly reduced from 72 paras as on 01.04.2009.
II. CENTRAL GOVERNMENT HEALTH SCHEME
Recommendation/Observation
1.8 Despite continuous under utilization of funds during the Eleventh Five Year Plan, there is
enhanced allocation in Plan funds from Rs. 78.00 crore in 2011-12 to Rs. 82.81 crore for 2012-13.
The Committee is given to understand that these enhanced funds are meant for meeting the
expenditure on account of salary and wages, purchase of medicines and all other administrative
expenses incurred by some CGHS cities for which budget is allocated under plan Head only  i.e.
Chandigarh, Bhopal, Bhubaneswar, Guwahati, Shillong, Dehradun, Jabalpur, Ranchi and
Thiruvananthapuram. Further, construction of own CGHS building where plots are already allotted
and opening of already sanctioned dispensaries in Delhi and NCR are also proposed during 2012-13.
The Committee observes that the Department has to undertake lot of ground work in CGHS and
is of the view that for this purpose the targets need to be set, resources to be placed at the
disposal in time and implementing agencies need to be made accountable for accomplishing the set
targets from the very outset. (Para 2.4)
Action Taken
The observation of the Hon’ble Committee to ensure maximum utilisation of funds is
accepted for compliance in the future.

5
Recommendation/Observation
1.9 The Committee notes that the earmarked funds for 2012-13 under the scheme are not in
tune with the projected demand of the Department. From the figures made available to the
Committee it is evident that Rs.600.00 crore have been allocated against projected demand of
Rs.759.08 crore under non Plan Head and Rs.82.81 crore against the projection of Rs.92.17 crore
under Plan head. The Committee is given to understand that this deficit in allocation may adversely
affect procurement of medicines. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Department
should try its best to convince the Planning Commission and Ministry of Finance, for enhancement
of allocation at RE stage for procurement of medicines. (Para 2.5)
Action Taken
Every effort is made to secure maximum fund for procurement of medicines. The Hon’ble
Committee’s suggestion is noted for compliance at the RE stage for enhancement of allocation
under the Plan head.
Recommendation/Observation
1.10 On a query regarding the settlement of reimbursement claims of CGHS beneficiaries, the
Committee has been apprised of a number of steps taken by the Department to expedite the process
and as a result thereof the pendency has been brought out significantly to 3075 bills all over the
country. The Committee lauds the efforts made by the Department to bring about a significant
reduction in pendency of reimbursement claims and hopes that the Department would strive to
bring this figure further down with its sincere efforts. The Committee likes the Department to issue
a circular intimating the simplified procedures and for dispelling any misgivings among the
beneficiaries. (Para 2.6)
Action Taken
The Hon’ble Committee has appreciated the efforts made by CGHS for addressing the
issues of Medical Reimbursement Claims (MRC). CGHS will keep on making the requisite efforts
to bring about further improvements in the MRC disposal and also to make the process hassle free
and fast for the beneficiaries. The circular issued in this regard has been placed on the CGHS
website – www.cghs.nic.in.
Recommendation/Observation
1.11 The Department has stated that in order to mitigate the problems faced by the CGHS
beneficiaries in getting their bills reimbursed, there is no need of verification of bills by the treating
doctor and submission of essentiality certificate. Also, specific guidelines for examination of
requests for full reimbursement of claims have also been issued. In addition to this, the
beneficiaries now have the option of submitting the original bills under any health insurance scheme

XV. NATIONAL MENTAL HEALTH PROGRAMME
Recommendation/Observation
1.37 The Committee is shocked to see the mismatch between requirement of manpower under
NMHP and the personnel actually available. The Department has also stated that there is shortage
of the qualified mental health manpower in the country. The Committee is unable to accept the
Department’s statement when so many efforts are being invested in strengthening and upgradation
of the institutions, training of personnel and research activities. Further, the Committee also notes
that the last National Survey of Mental Health Resources was carried out a decade back in 2002,
which clearly indicates casual attitude on part of Department in this matter. The Committee would
like to be apprised of whether the Department is taking any steps to conduct the next National
Mental Health Survey and parameters on the basis of which such surveys are carried out by the
Department. (Para 15.7)

16
Action Taken
It is admitted that there is an acute shortage of qualified professionals in the field of Mental
Health in the country which is also a major constraint in meeting the mental health needs and
providing optimal mental health services to the people. Due to shortage of manpower in mental
health, the implementation of the District Mental Health Programme in the country suffered
adversely in previous plan periods. To address the acute shortage of manpower in the field of
mental health, the Department started the Manpower Development Schemes under the National
Mental Health Programme. The scheme envisaged establishment of 11 Centres of Excellence in
Mental Health across the country and strengthening/establishment of 120 PG Departments in Mental
Health Specialties (30 each in Psychiatry, Clinical Psychology, Psychiatric Social Work and
Psychiatric Nursing).
Once fully operational, the Institutes funded under Manpower Development Schemes would
produce 1756 qualified professionals in the field of Mental Health every year as per details at
Annexure-IV .
The Department is also aware that in spite of implementing the Manpower Development
Schemes in the country, there is a great mismatch between requirement of manpower under NMHP
and the personnel actually available. In this regard, it is stated that once all the Centres of
Excellence and PG Departments become fully operational, only then 1756 qualified professionals
would be produced each year and consequently it will take time to bridge the gap between
availability and requirement of mental health professionals in the country. Also, steps would be
taken to further enhance the output capacity of the institutes in the future which will further
enhance the rate at which the gap would be bridged. The Ministry is planning to conduct a nation-
wide survey in the current year to assess the current situation of mental health resources in the
country.
Recommendation/Observation
1.38 Majority of districts in the country have not still been covered under DMHP, which was
initiated way back in 1996. Almost 16 years have passed but the scenario seems to be at standstill.
With about 500 districts still remaining outside the reach of this vital aspect of the programme, the
Committee can only hope that the matter regarding extension of District Mental Health Programme
to all the districts of India would be taken up earnestly during the Twelfth Five Year Plan and the
failure of the Department to extend the District MHP in the Tenth and Eleventh Plan would not
be repeated. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Department should make all out
efforts to accomplish all the set targets within the set time line. The Committee would like to be

XVIII. HEALTH SECTOR DISASTER PREPAREDNESS AND MANAGEMENT INCLUDING
EMERGENCY MEDICAL RELIEF
Recommendation/Observation
1.42 As regards the utilization status of allocated Plan funds and physical targets set and
achieved during 2011-12 under Programme, the Plan allocation at RE stage was reduced to Rs.2.00
crore from Rs.80.50 crore at BE stage. Further, the actual expenditure was even lesser to the tune
of Rs.0.02 crore. The reasons behind the reduction of funds at RE stage were due to a few
sporadic outbreaks in Avian & Pandemic Influenza which could be managed by drugs, personal
protective equipments etc. available in the stock. No fresh procurement was anticipated and no
large scale visual or print media publicity required. Also, in context to the Health Sector Disaster
Preparedness, as the specifications finalization took time, it was anticipated that the allocated budget
under this head would not be utilized. In addition to this, there has been no major disaster requiring
health sector intervention during the year 2011-12. However, the Committee is not convinced with
the reasons cited for not procuring one mobile Hospital due to the delay in refraining specification
by Technical Sub-Committee which truly reflect no-preparedness on the part of the Department.
The Committee, therefore, recommends the Department should even in the absence of any major
disaster, acquire all necessary equipments and create the required infrastructure in order to get it
fully equipped to face any disaster instead of waiting for the disaster to happen and then move
forward for getting prepared to face the same. Almost cent percent under utilisation of allocated
funds indicates lack of seriousness and lacklustre approach on the part of the Department for any
eventuality. (Para 18.2)
Action Taken
The proposed 100 bed Mobile Hospital is state of art, all weather, selfcontained mobile
hospital designed to provide secondary/tertiary level medical, surgical and critical care at or near
disaster site. It can be airlifted or mobilized through rail or road. It is a full-fledged hospital with
support systems including diagnostic and imaging facilities, kitchen, sanitation, water treatment
plant etc. Laying down specifications for over hundreds of equipments, instruments and
customizing it to Indian conditions, took time. Now that the specifications have been finalized, the
procurement would be expedited to follow the guidance given by the Committee. However, this
would require engaging specialized agencies with expertise in international bidding, having know
how of such systems, evaluation and pre-dispatch inspection, installation and commissioning.
Mobile hospital is a component of a broader plan for disaster preparedness in health sector.
All pre-project activities have been completed and the implementation is under process.
Recommendation/Observation
1.43 The Committee welcomes and appreciates the aforesaid initiatives proposed to be taken by
the Department during the Twelfth Plan. The Committee infers that these measures would certainly
help in building a taskforce to strengthen the facilities to be utilized at the time of emergency during
disaster subject to the condition that these are implemented in letter and spirit. The proposals of
capacity development for medical intervention in various types of disasters and developing

XXI. NA TIONAL TOBACCO CONTROL PROGRAMME
Recommendation/Observation
2.17 The Committee notes with regret that the allocations made at BE stage was reduced
drastically at RE stage during the entire Eleventh Plan period except the year 2008-09. The
Committee fails to comprehend the reasons for same. However, the Department could optimally
utilize nearly complete reduced allocations made at RE stage. The Committee also feels that a lot
more needs to be done to eliminate the scourge of Tobacco related diseases and Department
should make all out efforts to utilize entire allocations made at BE stage for the year 2012-13.
(Para 21.3)
Action Taken
The allocations made at BE stage have been reduced at RE stage mainly on account of the
fact that the tobacco product testing laboratories could not be set up during the Eleventh Plan due
to various issues such as approval for manpower, procurement of machinery, trainings for staff
and accreditation from NABL for tobacco testing etc. These issues have now been sorted out and
it is expected that the tobacco testing labs will be set up in 2012-13.
Further, some of the States did not furnish the Utilization Certificates and Statements of
Expenditure, due to which further release of the Grants-in-Aid could not be made to them every
year.

30
The Ministry agrees with the view of the Committee that more needs to be done to
eliminate the scourge of tobacco related disease. The Ministry has plans to upscale the programme
in the Twelfth Plan with coverage of all States and districts in phases. The Ministry is also looking
at improvement of the programme components, and its integration to the national programmes on
prevention and control of non-communicable diseases (NCDs) so as to have better outcomes and
synergy, since tobacco is the biggest risk factor for NCDs. The Ministry is also taking up various
other activities in this regard such as issue of guidelines, taking up the implementation of ban on
Gutka with the States, notification of new pictorial health warnings on smoking forms of tobacco,
setting up a national tobacco quitline with a toll free number, changes in the reporting format and
introduction of web-based reporting and feedback system to improve monitoring, visits to States
and districts to follow up implementation of NTCP and compliance with COTPA 2003 at the State/
district level, capacity building through regional workshops and trainings, advocacy workshops with
policy makers and law enforcers etc. at the State level, conducting national review workshop,
strengthening of anti-tobacco helpline through introduction of a webbased reporting system for
registration of complaints against violations of antitobacco law and their dissemination to the state
and district focal points, sustained media and outdoor campaigns with a strategic media plan,
Interministerial consultations for implementation of WHO FCTC guidelines (under Articles 17 and 18)
and the draft treaty on illicit trade in tobacco products (under Article 15).
Recommendation/Observation
2.18 The Committee had commented in its previous reports on the issue of the setting up of
National Tobacco Regulatory Authority and Tobacco Testing Labs. As per the information supplied
by the Department, the former is still at discussion stage while there has been some progress made
regarding the latter. The Committee, while appreciating the efforts made by the Department on the
issue of setting up of Tobacco Testing Laboratories, expresses its displeasure at the laggard
approach taken by Department on the matter of setting up of National Tobacco Regulatory
Authority (NTRA). The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Department should prepare a
blueprint by the time the said authority would be set up and keep the Committee regularly updated
of the progress made in this regard. (Para 21.4)
Action Taken
Currently three models for setting up NTRA are under discussion:
MODEL-I: The NTRA may be established through a notification under the provisions of
Section 25 read with Section 31(1) of Cigarette and Tobacco Products (Prohibition of
Advertisement and Regulation of Trade and Commerce, Production, Supply and Distribution) Act
(COTPA), 2003. However, NTRA formed through this process will be non-statutory.
MODEL-II: The NTRA may be established through an Act of Parliament by amending the
COTPA, wherein provisions of State level authorities; quasijudicial action; penalty provisions,
speedy trials by Special Courts etc. may be incorporated.
MODEL-III: A hybrid model wherein the NTRA may be notified through Rules issued
under COTPA, and steps may be initiated for establishing a statutory body through amendment to
COTPA 2003.
It is felt that instead of creating a new body, the existing infrastructure of the Food Safety
Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) could be used for the purpose, which can perform the
functions envisioned under NTRA. The rationale for this stand was that creation of a separate
infrastructure for NTRA would be a time taking process, and hence the most feasible option would
be to create NTRA as a sub-ordinate structure/office under FSSAI. However FSSAI has conveyed

31
its reservations saying that not all tobacco products listed in the Schedule to COTPA 2003 can be
classified as food products as per definitions under the Food Safety Standards Act 2006, and hence
NTRA cannot qualify to be a part of FSSAI. The matter is under further discussion with FSSAI
and within the Ministry to take a final view in the matter

Recommendation/Observation

Action Taken
The Central Government has taken following steps to monitor the expenditure made by the
beneficiary medical colleges under the scheme for strengthening and upgradation of State
Government medical colleges:
(i) Instructions being issued from time to time to the medical colleges for sending the
monthly progress report along with the details of work done and other necessary
documents;
(ii) Requested the State Government authorities to monitor the progress made by the
medical colleges.
(iii) Periodic meeting with the representatives of State Governments and medical colleges.
(iv) On the spot evaluation made by the Central Government teams.
For the purpose of monitoring and the smooth implementation of the schemes, the Central
Government has directed the medical colleges to submit the monthly progress report, bank account
statement reconciled with the expenditure, utilization certificate, audit report, list of equipments and

colleges. The State Governments have also been requested to monitor the progress and expenditure

the State Government officials and Dean/Principal of the medical colleges to review the progress and
to ensure that funds be utilized by the medical colleges at the earliest so that 2nd installment can
be released to medical colleges in time. Besides, the teams from Central Government also visited
some medical colleges of the States of Rajasthan, Orissa, Assam, Gujarat and Goa to see the actual
physical progress made by the medical colleges out of the Central Government funds and requested

32
the college authorities to expedite the work so that the aim of increasing seats under the scheme
can be achieved.
Under the present scheme, a total of Rs.501.00 crore has been released to 72 medical
colleges during 2009-10, 2010-11 and 2011-12. Out of these 72 medical colleges, 40 medical
colleges have received state matching share which amounts to Rs.106.719 crore (approximately).
There are 33 medical colleges which are in the process of utilizing the funds and are sending
monthly progress report to the Ministry. As per the information provided by these medical colleges,

As regards north eastern States, it is stated that the Central Government funded 03 medical

Regarding Agartala Government Medical College, Agartala, Tripura, it is stated that as per

I. BUDGETARY ALLOCATION
Recommendation/Observation
3.1 The Committee observes that a shortfall in allocation of funds to the tune of Rs.10507.53
crore vis-à-vis the proposed outlay for 2012-13 that too at a time when the Government has
committed itself to raising its expenditure on health from roughly 1% of the GDP to 2.5% of the
GDP by the end of Twelfth Plan is baffling, to say the least. The public expenditure on health in
the country is one of the lowest in the world and total plan expenditure would need to rise
substantially and consistently before the target expenditure level of 2.5% of GDP is achieved. The
Committee, therefore, desires to know the reasons behind the substantially reduced allocation for
2012-13. The Committee also desires to know the rate at which the total Plan expenditure would
need to grow annually, in order to meet the expenditure level of 2.5% of GDP by the end of the
Twelfth Plan and what would be the share of the Centre and the States therein. The Committee,
therefore, recommends that the Department should make all out efforts to convince the Planning
Commission and the Department of Expenditure for enhancing the annual Plan allocation for the
remaining four years of the Twelfth Plan and also at RE 2012-13 in such a way that the target
of meeting expenditure level of 2.5% of GDP could be achieved. (Para 1.6)
Action Taken
3.2 The approach paper to Twelfth Five Year Plan envisages an increase in total public health
expenditure to 2.5% of GDP by the end of Twelfth Plan. The outlay of both Centre and States
on health would need to be enhanced progressively to achieve the target of 2.5% of GDP. The
States account for approximately two-thirds of the total expenditure. Frontloading of financing of
activities envisaged for Twelfth Plan would be needed for meeting the timelines for the achievement
of target. Department is engaging with Planning Commission to approve the outlay as proposed by
this Department for the Twelfth Five Year Plan and enhance the annual plan allocation for the
remaining four years of the Twelfth Plan. The Committee’s recommendations that Department
should make all out efforts to convince Department of Expenditure for enhancing allocation at RE
2012-13 has been noted for compliance.
Further recommendation
3.3 The Department had been asked to address two pointed queries regarding the
reasons for reduced allocation for 2012-13 and the required rate of increase in Total Plan
allocation to meet the expenditure level of 2.5 per cent of GDP. However, the Committee
is constrained to note that the Department reply is evasive in as much as it fails to shed
light on these queries. The Committee would like the Department to exercise greater care
and precautions while framing its reply in future and also furnish the requisite
information.
33

34
Recommendation/Observation
3.4 From the information made available, the Committee gathers that some of the major
programmes/heads which are likely to be affected due to substantially less allocation of funds
include PMSSY , Financial Assistance for Strengthening and Upgradation of Medical Colleges,
Establishment of New Medical Colleges in underserved States, Strengthening of tertiary care
institutions like AIIMS, JIPMER, PGIMER, NIMHANS, Safdarjung Hospital and VMMC, RML
Hospital, NPCDSC, Capacity Building for establishing Trauma Care Facilities in Government
Hospitals on National Highways and the proposed National Urban Health Mission. The Committee
is of the firm opinion that the above trend of allocation of funds would adversely impact the public
health sector’s ability to cater to the healthcare needs of the people at large. The Committee is also
aware that the absorption capacity of the States has witnessed improvement and their spending
capacity is expected to pick up during the Twelfth Plan. Besides, presently more than 9 crore
people of the country have been categorized as urban poor, mostly residing in urban slums. The
level of availability of health care facilities to these poor people is worse than that available to the
rural poor. Their health indicators are also worse than those of the rural poor. The Committee,

of funds would further impact the health indicators of poor people residing in urban slums.
(Para 1.9)
Action Taken
The views expressed by the Committee have been noted. Launching of National Urban
Health Mission (NUHM) is one of the priorities in Twelfth Plan for dealing with health issue of
urban poor. An allocation of Rs.23452 crore has been proposed for NUHM in the Twelfth Plan.
Availability of the required resources is the pre-requisite for starting the NUHM.
Recommendation/Observation

3.9 The Committee’s attention has been drawn to faulty planning of the National Programme for
Prevention and Control of Cancer, Diabetes, Cardiovascular Diseases and Stroke (NPCDCS). The

35
Committee was informed that NPCDCS was launched in 2010 in 100 districts across 21 States.
Under Cancer component of NPCDCS, various activities like early diagnosis of cancer,
chemotherapy facilities etc. were envisaged. However, non-availability of adequate manpower, non-

The programme also envisaged strengthening of Government Medical College Hospitals including
erstwhile Regional Cancer Centers across the country as Tertiary Cancer Centre (TCC) for providing
comprehensive Cancer care services. These institutions are eligible for financial assistance unto
Rs.6.00 crore (Rs.4.80 crore from Central Government and Rs.1.20 crore from State Government.)
Out of the 21 States, this Ministry released Rs.7.09 crore during 2010-11 to Health
Societies of 19 States (except UP and Jharkhand as they had not furnished Bank Details) with the
condition that the States have to furnish the MoU urgently to this Ministry and the States should
credit their share of 20% in respect of District Cancer Care Facility sub-scheme of NPCDCS.

furnishing of SOE/UC by the State Health Societies in respect of previous grant-in-aid released

Further, we had not received anticipated proposals (complete in all respects) for Financial
Assistance under the Tertiary Cancer Centre (TCC) Scheme of NPCDCS. Besides this, the shortfall
of expenditure by around Rs.10 crore w.r.t. RE is due to furnishing of incomplete proposals without
the approval of Governing Body by CNCI. Therefore, the BE (Plan) Allocation of Rs.200 crore was
reduced to Rs.112 crore at the RE and the utilized amount was Rs.99.79 crore.

3.11 While making the above recommendation, the Committee had expected the
