in aid to the State Health Societies/NGOs to ensure that the amount allocated is utilized
judiciously and scrupulously. (Para 5.16)
National Leprosy Eradication Programme (NLEP)
The Committee observes that the problem of unspent balances with States has been
continuing for years together. Instead of analysing the real reasons behind unspent balances
and taking corrective action accordingly, the Department seems to be adopting routine and
passive attitude and letting things drift, which is a matter of serious concern. Removing the
impediments in way of financial performance is an imminent necessity in the interest of
achieving the targets under NLEP. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the
Department should analyse the reasons behind the continuing trend of unspent balances and
tackle the problem accordingly, and not continue disbursing grants in a routine manner
even when these are not being utilised. (Para 5.20)
The Department has further informed that against the projected outlay of Rs. 787
Crores for the Twelfth Plan under the National Leprosy Eradication Programme, the
approved outlay has been only Rs. 500 Crores. The Committee would like to be apprised of
the impact of reduced allocation under the Programme. The Committee would also like
to be informed of State-wise break-up of newly detected cases of leprosy during the year
2012-13. (Para 5.21)
The Committee would like to be informed since when the survey is being conducted,
whether any time-frame had been set up for conclusion of the survey and whether any delay
has taken place in submission of the report. The Committee also desires to be informed of
the findings of the Report when submitted and action taken thereon. (Para 5.23)
National Trachoma and Blindness Control Programme (NTBCP)
From the data given above there seems to be a wide gap in the physical as well as
the financial performance. Huge mismatch between the targets achieved vis-a-vis the
targets set suggests that the programme did not achieve the intended objective. Such kind
of deviations are also indicative of the fact that the monitoring mechanism was slack and

97
also that the targets set were not backed by any action plan to achieve them. The
Committee would expect the Department not to feel complacent by merely fixing the targets
but formulation of sound action plans in coordination with State Governments to accomplish
the same. The Committee also desires that the achievements of the set targets be assessed
objectively and the reasons for the shortfall analysed in detail for formulating remedial
measures for proper implementation thereof. The Committee also desires that a review of
the implementation of the scheme may be done at the earliest. (Para 5.26)
The Committee is of the view that in a resource constrained country like India
greater attention needs to be paid on health outcomes than health outlays. The Committee
would, therefore, like the Department to brace itself for targeted action for satisfactory
physical performance of the above programme during 2013-14. The Committee would like
to be apprised of the achievements made in respect of the above activities vis-a-vis targets
set therefor. The Committee also is given to understand that in some cases of cataract
operation, people have lost vision and/or developed complications. Therefore, organisations
implementing the programme should be asked to follow and adhere the norms and
procedures. Government may prepare guidelines in this regard. (Para 5.28)
In reply to a query, the Department has informed that at least 400 Multi Purpose District
Opthalmic Units covering nearly all the districts are proposed to be set up during the Twelfth
Plan subject to approval and availability of funds. The Committee would like to be informed
whether necessary approval could be obtained to the above proposal and if so, whether any
roadmap for setting up of the Opthalmic Units has been chalked out. (Para 5.29)
National Iodine Deficiency Disorders Control Programme (NIDDCP)
This is yet another case of great variation between Budgetary Estimates, Revised
Estimates and actual expenditure incurred by the Department which reflects poorly on its
budgetary planning. The Committee urges upon the Department to assess requirement of
funds more realistically so that the budgeted funds do not get blocked and surrendered
later. (Para 5.31)
The Committee was informed that funds would be provided to the Salt
Commissioner’s Office for quality control of iodized salt at production level during the
Twelfth Plan. The Committee would like to be apprised of the role of the Salt Commissioner
in ensuring quality control of iodized salt at production level and the role to be played by
the Department in ensuring quality control of iodized salt at production level. (Para 5.33)
National Integrated Disease Surveillance Programme (NIDSP)
The Committee is utterly disappointed on the reasons adduced by the Department for
under utilisation of funds viz. ‘unavailability of Utilisation Certificates from States’, ‘vacant
contractual positions in the States’. There are serious shortcomings in the role played by
the Department in acting as a facilitator in implementing NIDSP in coordination with the
State Governments. The Committee expects that Department would introspect and the
shortcomings noticed would be sorted out in the right earnest to fulfil and the intended
objective of NIDSP. The Committee also recommends that States may be impressed upon
the need to fill up vacant the contractual positions at the earliest. (Para 5.35)
The Committee notes that a substantial allocation of Rs. 640.39 crore has been
made for NIDSP for the Twelfth Plan. Given the fact that there has been persistent
under-utilisation of the allocated funds under IDSP during the last many years, the

98
Committee urges upon the Department to put in place a rigorous mechanism for
improving utilisation level of allocated provision for the purpose so that the desired
results are achieved. (Para 5.38)
The Committee notes that a decentralized laboratory based IT-enabled disease
surveillance system is targeted to be strengthened/maintained during the Twelfth Plan.
Since there is already a delay of one year in finalizing the Twelfth Plan, the Committee
wonders as to how the envisaged objective would be achieved in the remaining four years.
The Committee desires that early action may be taken in this regard. A comprehensive road
map may be prepared for implementation of NIDSP programme during Twelfth Plan period.
(Para 5.39)
The Committee while welcoming the conversion of IDSP from a Central Sector Scheme
to Centrally Sponsored Scheme, i.e. NIDSP, observes that the Department is required to play
a major role in facilitating IT-based data reporting through portal. (Para 5.41)
VI. Reproductive and Child Health Project (RCHP)
For the FY 2013-14, a total of Rs. 60 crores has been allocated at BE stage for RCH
procurement. The same will be utilized for procurement of sanitary napkins under the Menstrual
Hygiene scheme.  The Committee would like to know the manner in which the sanitary
napkins under the Menstrual Hygiene Scheme would be procured and distributed. Whether
the allocated funds would be adequate to meet the requirement of the vast country like
India. In case the allocated funds is not adequate, the Department should seek addition of
fund at RE stage. (Para 6.4)
VII. Routine Immunization Programme
The Committee notes that an amount of Rs. 168.17 crore which was an Externally Aided
component, had to be surrendered at RE 2012-13 stage due to non-procurement of cold chain
items. The Committee strongly deprecates such kind of inefficiencies and would like to know
whether any commitment charges had to be paid on the surrended amount of external aid. The
Committee feels that the reasons like delay in signing agreements between the Government of
India and the various stakeholders is not a reasonable justification for reducing the funds at
RE stage and especially given the importance of cold chains in the Immunization programme.
The Committee feels that the surrendering of budgeted funds could have been easily avoided
had the Department undertaken due diligence well in advance and ensured time bound signing
and execution of the agreements. The Committee strongly recommends the Department not to
repeat this lapse in future and take all precautions to complete all formalities well in advance
for the success of this ambitious life saving programme. (Para 7.2)
The Committee feels that the Department has not been able to keep pace with the
reduced funds allocated at even the RE Stage as can be seen from the fact that out of
Rs.591.76 crores allocated at RE stage, the utilization figures, as on 31.03.2013, is
Rs. 454.83 crore. The Committee feels that keeping the funds idly parked year after year,
is deplorable as the same could have been gainfully utilized for some other fund-starved
schemes/ projects. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Department should
strive to adhere to the fund utilization targets well in time in order to ensure that the
allocated funds in the future are not pruned down due to fiscal inefficiencies thereby
affecting the ambitious life saving programme like immunization. (Para 7.4)
The Committee takes strong exception to the large unspent balances/savings
especially due to delay in introduction of Pentavalent vaccine which would result in

99
jeopardizing the health and well being of the children and recommends that the Department
should adopt a more proactive approach to ensure prevention of delays in introduction of
Pentavalent vaccine. (Para 7.6)
The Committee notes that though the Department seems to be patting itself on its
back for achievement during the year 2012-13, these are well short of the set targets. The
Committee would, therefore, like the Department to analyse the contributory factor for
under-achievement of the targets and initiate remedial measures accordingly. (Para 7.7)
VIII. Pulse Polio Immunization
The Committee is appreciative of the fact that the Department has done a yeoman
service in achieving a near elimination of the polio virus. However, the Committe impresses
upon the Department not to lower its guard and maintain a high level of vigilance through
survelliance across the country for detection of polio cases. (Para 8.4)
The Committee impresses upon the Department to ensure that effective surveillance
measures are taken by it to prevent any importation or circulation of wild polio virus from
the neighbouring countries. (Para 8.6)
IX. Mission Flexible Pool
The Committee notes that occurrence of huge savings/unspent balances under
Mission Flexible Pool has been a recurrent feature year after year. The Committee is not
aware of the underlying causes of the savings/ unspent balances. The Committee would
therefore, like the Department to get the Mission evaluated by an independent agency and
take remedial measures to overcome the lapses. The Committee would also like to know
whether the fund under the Mission Flexible Pool flow through the treasury route or
society route. (Para 9.3)
The Committee would like the Department to set realistic targets for the above
activities and hold periodic review meetings to ensure that concrete results are achieved and
there is little scope for the budgeted funds remaining unutilized. (Para 9.5)
Upgradation of PHCs/CHCs
Upgradation of PHCs and CHCs which are to be upgraded to First Referral Units
(FRUs) is a major component under Mission Flexible Pool. The Department has informed
that the number of First Referral Units (FRUs) has increased significantly from 940 in 2005
to 2562 in 2012-13. The Committee would like to be informed of State-wise targets set for
upgradation of PHCs and CHCs to FRUs and the achievements made in respect thereof
during 2012-13. The Committee would also like to be apprised of the targets set for 2013-14,
State-wise. (Para 9.6)
The Committee welcomes the proposal for skill development of ASHAs and desires
to be kept apprised of the final outcome of the initiatives taken by the Department for
their skill development and career progression. (Para 9.11)
The Committee is aware of the fact that ASHAs have proven to be a vital link
between the doctor and the ANM. However there have been reports that remuneration to
ASHA is very meagre and requires to be suitably enhanced. The Committee would,
therefore, like the Department to expedite its decision on revising incentives for ASHAs and
to make it commensurate with her job responsibilities. (Para 9.13)

100
X. RCH Flexible Pool
The Committee feels that the adage that ‘I have miles to go before I sleep’ aptly
describes the situation of the targets set vis-a-vis the achievements so far in case of IMR,
MMR and TFR. The Committee notes that countries in almost similar situations such as
Bangladesh, Brazil, China, Sri Lanka have performed much better than India. What is of
more concern to the Committee that at the present pace of decline, it would be difficult to
achieve the targets in respect of IMR, MMR and TFR even by 2015. The Committee,
therefore, recommends that the Department sets monitorable targets for expansion of
activities envisaged under RCH Flexi-Pool on a wide-scale and make concerted efforts to
reduce MMR, IMR and TFR. (Para 10.4)
The Committee also recommends that the strategies adopted to achieve the goals of
reduction in MMR, IMR and TFR need to be evaluated afresh so that corrective measures
are taken. (Para 10.5)
The Committee, while appreciating the special initiatives being taken to reduce
under-five mortality, feels that these initiatives would be more effective if these are clubbed
together under one umbrella to dispense with multiplicity of authorities and to mitigate the
ultimate beneficiary from the maze of initiatives presently being undertaken. The
Committee, therefore, recommends to bring all these initiatives under one umbrella to
ensure optimum benefits to the ultimate beneficiary. The Committee would also like to
impress upon the Department to specifically map the girl child who expires before attaining
the age of five, as the real reason for less than five mortality rate is due to the rampant
female infanticide prevalent in the country. (Para 10.7)
XI. MILLENIUM DEVELOPMENT GOALS (MDG) (PERTAINING TO HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE)
The Committee feels that the success rate of achievements with regard to Millenium
Development Goals has been a mixed bag of success. While the department is more or less
on track with respect to MDG-4 and MDG-5, the success rate in respect of MDG-6 seems
a distant dream especially with regard to the viral diseases like Dengue, Chikungunya
which is a constant cause of worry year after year, not to mention new diseases like H1N1
which have now started spreading across the country. The Department should, therefore, put
in place a ‘Dedicated Sentinel Force’ whose main protocol would be ensuring prevention of
entry of diseases from outside the borders(land, sea, air) of the country. Additionally, the
Committee feels that the Department should explore the possibility of tapping the additional
resources for mopping up additional funds for its various programmes particularly for the
welfare of our poverty ridden masses. (Para 11.5)
XII. IMPLEMENTATION OF NRHM (PHASE-I)
From perusal of the above, the Committee finds that the major problem in
implementation of the NRHM (Phase-I) stems from lack of adequate infrastructure/
manpower in the States/UTs, which has a direct impact on the implementation of the
Mission on the whole. The Committee, while welcoming the initiatives being taken by the
Department to increase involvement of the States, feel that the Department should first
and foremost focus on ensuring opening of more medical colleges, district hospitals, GNM/
ANM schools without further delay along with ensuring that such colleges/schools are
opened on equitable distribution throughout the country so as to ensure that the
Department’s Goal to ensure Universal Health Coverage is implemented in both letter and
spirit. (Para 12.2)

101
The Committee would like to be apprised of the Guidelines framed for NGOs
involvement in the various programmes under NRHM and whether there have been any
instances of blacklisting of NGOs during implementation of NRHM(Phase-I). The Committee
also recommends that while pursuing welfare measures through the NGOs, the Department
should also emphasize on recruiting more ANMs/GNMs, so as to ensure more focused
implementation of various Schemes in the rural areas during the second Phase of NRHM.
(Para 12.5)
XIII. NEW SCHEMES DURING THE TWELFTH PLAN
The Committee, while being appreciative of the New Schemes being launched during
the Twelfth Plan, would like the Department to focus aggressively on provision of free
generic drugs as the high Out of Pocket Expenditure still remains a major cause of concern
for the vast majority of people in the country. The Committee also impress that the
Department should also encourage production of more generic drugs, as manufacture of
Generic Drugs by the Department and free provision of the same by the Government would
reduce the high Out of Pocket Expenses that a vast majority of the people still bear with.
(Para 13.3)

REPORT
I. INTRODUCTION
1.1 The Department of Indian Systems of Medicine and Homoeopathy (ISM&H) was established
under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare in March, 1995. It was renamed as Department
of Ayurveda, Yoga and Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha and Homoeopathy (AYUSH) in November, 2003.
The Department under its purview has two Regulatory Councils, five Research Councils, seven
National Institutes, two North Eastern Institutes, All India institute of Ayurveda, two Pharmacopeia
Laboratories, a National Medicinal Plants Board and a public sector undertaking for manufacture of
Ayurveda and Unani medicines. Pharmacopeia Commission, Pharmacopeia Committees and Drugs
Technical Advisory Board for Ayurveda, Siddha, Unani and Homeopathy drugs are set up to evolve
technical standards and policy directives and advise the Government in matters of quality control
and regulation of drugs. The Department is responsible for policy formulation, development and
implementation of programmes for the growth, development and propagation of Ayurveda, Yoga and
Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha and Homeopathy (AYUSH) systems of Health Care. Sowa Rigpa is the
recent addition to the existing family of AYUSH systems.
1.2 The outlay of the Department has increased from Rs.88.00 crore in the Eighth Plan to
Rs.3988.00 crores in the Eleventh Plan. The total allocation for the Department for the Twelfth
Plan is Rs.10044.00 crore.
1.3 The Twelfth Plan recognizes that the strengths of Indian Systems of Medicine and
Homeopathy, if suitably used, can help advance the goals of the Twelfth Plan. AYUSH systems
would be main-streamed using their areas of strengths namely in preventive and promotive health
care, diseases and health conditions relating to women and children, older persons, NCDs, mental
ailments, stress management, palliative care, rehabilitation and health promotion.
1.4 To rationalize the various schemes with the measures of modification, viz. ,
(i) discontinuation of some schemes, (ii) introduction of some schemes and (iii) merger/
consolidation of some major schemes, it has been decided as follows:–
(a) To discontinue the following schemes from 2013-14 and onwards:
(i) Cataloguing, Digitization, etc. of Manuscripts and Development of AYUSH IT
Tools, Applications and Networks.
(ii) Funding of NGOs engaged in local Health traditions/midwifery practices etc.
under AYUSH.
1.5 However, budgetary provision has been made for the two schemes in the financial year
2013-14 for meeting committed liabilities/second and subsequent installment of ongoing projects.
(b) To shift the following new schemes from the scheme head to Sub-Scheme head:
(i) All India Institute of Yoga (under the Scheme: System Strengthening)
(ii) All India Institute of Homoeopathy (under the Scheme: System Strengthening)
(iii) All India Institute of Unani Medicine (under the Scheme: System Strengthening)
(iv) Homoeopathy Medicines Pharmaceutical Co. Ltd (under the Scheme: System
Strengthening)
(v) National Institute of Medicinal Plants (under the Scheme: Educational Institutes)

2
(vi) National Institute of Sowa Rigpa
(vii) Indian Institute of AYUSH Pharmaceutical Sciences (under the scheme:
Educational Institutes)
(viii) Central Council for Research in Sowa Rigpa (Under the scheme: Research and
Development including medicinal plants)
(ix) National Commission for Human Resources in AYUSH (under the scheme: HRD)
(x) AYUSH Gram (under the scheme: Promotion of AYUSH)
(xi) National AYUSH Health Programme (under the scheme: Promotion of AYUSH).
(c) To introduce the following new schemes as recommended/decided by the National
Development Council:
(i) National Institute on Geriatrics (under the scheme: Educational Institutes)
(ii) National Institute on Metabolic and Lifestyle Diseases (under the scheme:
Educational Institutes)
(iii) National Institute for Drug and Tobacco De-addiction (under the scheme:
Educational Institutes).
1.6 After the above exercise, the total on-going main schemes became fourteen (Central Sector
- Eleven and Centrally Sponsored - three) and total schemes and sub-schemes became 60. The list
of schemes are as follows:
(i) System Strengthening
(ii) Educational Institutions
(iii) Research and Development including Medicinal Plants
(iv) HRD (Training Programme/Fellowship/Exposure visit/Upgradation of skills etc.)
(v) Cataloguing, Digitization etc. of Manuscripts and Development of AYUSH IT Tools,
Applications and Networks
(vi) International Co-operation
(vii) Development of AYUSH Industry
(viii) Funding of NGOs engaged in local Health traditions/midwifery practices etc. under
AYUSH
(ix) Pharmacovigilance initiative for ASU drugs

2.4 On being asked as to what steps have been taken by the Department to handle the
constraints faced in optimal utilization of the approved outlays, the Department in a written
submission stated the following:
“In order to identify the constraints being faced in optimal utilization of approved outlays,
the Department is getting the independent evaluation of its all schemes done. The report of
independent evaluation is awaited. In the meanwhile, the Department, based on its own
experience, has identified the following constraints and taken following remedial measures:–
(a) Most of the State Governments do not have separate institutional structure for
implementing Centrally Sponsored schemes of Department of AYUSH and whatever
structure is existing, is having capacity constraints in terms of human and other resources.
Action Taken
As a short term measure, this Department is providing financial assistance for setting
up Project Management Unit in each State which will facilitate implementation of the
Centrally Sponsored Schemes for Development of AYUSH Hospitals and Dispensaries in the
States.
(b) Pendency of Utilization Certificate is high in most of the States.
Action Taken
(i) HFM had written DO letters twice to the State Chief Ministers urging them to give
them personal attention in submission of pending UCs.
(ii) Secretary-AYUSH has written letter to the Chief Secretaries of the respective States/
UTs seeking their assistance to improve the financial flow from the Department of AYUSH
to their States and to liquidate the pending UCs.
(iii) The Secretary-AYUSH held three review meetings in 2011-12 and three review
meetings during 2012-13. States were repeatedly impressed upon to take effective and
expeditious measures for utilization of Grant-in-aid provided by the Department of AYUSH.
States were asked to take corrective measures.
(iv) Department has already identified the nodal officers in the Department to interact with
the State Governments and resolve the issues with them.
(c) Most of the proposals received from State Governments are not accompanied with
matching commitment from the State Government and the Project Implementation Plans
(PIPs) submitted are deficient.
Action taken
Department has developed standard pro-forma for submitting PIP and officers of this
Department also assist the State Government Authorities for submitting eligible and
acceptable proposals.

Comprehensive evaluation is also being undertaken in respect of all the schemes to

2.5 The Committee is concerned to note that except for the year 2010-11, the total actual
expenditure has invariably been considerably lower than Budget Estimates, particularly in
2011-12 and 2012-13. For Example, the total actual expenditure for the year 2008-09 was
Rs.471.13 crore against Budget Estimates (BE) of Rs. 534.00 crore; for the year 2009-10,
Rs.678.97 crore as against BE of Rs.734.00 crore; for the year 2011-12, Rs.611.46 crore as
against BE of 900.00 crore; and for the year 2012-13, Rs.580.27 crore as against BE of
Rs.990.00 crore. The Committee is not happy with this recurrent and persistent under
utilization of plan funds allocated for the Department. The Committee is constrained to
observe that such a persistent shortfall in the utilization of plan funds is indicative of fiscal
indiscipline and serious shortcoming in formulating the Budget Estimates. The Committee
in its 55
th Report on Demands for Grants (2012-13) of the Department had recommended to
take measures for exercising greater fiscal prudence. However, underutilization of the funds
to the tune of Rs.409.73 crore vis-a-vis BE for 2012-13 indicates that the Committee’s advice
was not heeded to. The Committee, therefore, even at the cost of repetition, strongly
recommends that concrete measures be taken to exercise utmost fiscal discipline and
ensure absorption of the allocated funds.
2.6 The Committee notes that the extent of surrendered funds is substantially higher
under Centrally Sponsored Schemes (30.9% with reference to RE) than that under Central
Sector Schemes (7.8% with reference to RE). The Committee also takes note of the
remedial steps for better absorption of funds but is not impressed by the half measures
taken by the Department to overcome the sub-optimal utilization of Plan funds as it is
obvious that these efforts have not yielded the desired results. In view of the fact that the
allocations have persistently remained under-utilized in the past several years, the
Department should have undertaken a comprehensive analysis in this regard and taken
corrective measures accordingly. Now that an evaluation of all the Schemes is being done
by an independent agency, the Committee is sanguine that the corrective measures will be
initiated for ensuring optimal and judicious utilization of the budgeted funds. The
Committee recommends that the evaluation be completed in a time-bound manner. The
Committee desires to be apprised of the outcome of the independent evaluation and action
taken thereon. The Committee would also like the Department to devise ways to evaluate
the impact of its various schemes. The Committee, simultaneously, impresses upon the
Department to be more prudent in their budget formulation and project their fund
requirements in a more realistic manner after timely collection of all the information
pertaining to fund requirements from the State Governments.
2.7 The Committee notes that a provision of Rs.1069.00 crore has been made in B.E
2013-14 on the plan side. The Committee would expect the Department to initiate concrete
measures at least from this year onwards to ensure that the sanctioned funds are
administered in a more diligent manner. The Committee desires to be kept apprised of the
steps taken for more efficient deployment and utilization of the funds budgeted for 2013-14.
2.8 The Committee also takes note of the fact that the share of AYUSH in the total
health outlay has been substantially enhanced to Rs.10044.00 crore in the Twelfthth Plan,
which is an increase of 235.47% over the actual expenditure of Eleventh Plan of Rs.2994.00
crore. The Committee is aware that health needs of a vast and diverse country like India
cannot be met by a single healthcare system and AYUSH health care systems have a very
vital role to play in expanding the outreach of health care to the people because of their
inherent advantages in terms of diversity, modest cost, low level of technological input, etc.

6
Indian system of medicines and traditional medicines should be complementary to Modern
system of Medicine. It is in this context that the Committee welcomes the enhanced
allocation of funds for AYUSH in the Twelfth Plan. The Committee also appreciates the
efforts made by the Department in getting enhanced allocation for the year 2013-14 inspite
of the fact that there was considerable underutilization of funds during the previous year
i.e. 2012-13. Persistent underutilization of funds to such extent is a serious concern for the
Committee. The Committee is also apprehensive about the utilization of such enhanced
allocation in 2013-14. Therefore, the Committee would expect the Department to put in
place a dedicated mechanism for stricter expenditure monitoring and financial discipline so
that the scarce resources do not remain locked up and surrendered later.

be made about the efficacy of the plan.

III. UPDATION OF CENTRAL REGISTERS OF INDIAN MEDICINE AND HOMOEOPATHY
3.1 The updation of Central Registers of Indian Medicine and Homoeopathy has constantly been
engaging the attention of the Committee. On being asked about the updated status of updation of
Central Registers of Indian Medicine and Homoeopathy and whether all the States have sent their
updated registers, the Department has furnished the following information (Annexure).
3.2 The Committee is not happy to note that despite its recommendation made in its 55
th
Report on Demands for Grants (2012-13) of the Department that all such information
should be made available in the public domain in an updated form on the touch of a button,
little progress seems to have been made in this regard, which is evident from the fact that
out of 23 States in respect of which information pertaining to updation of Central Register
of Indian Medicine has been made available, eight States are lagging behind in sending
updated information. As regards the Status of updation of the Central Register of
Homoeopathy, the Committee is surprised to note that in three cases, i.e.; Bihar, Tamil
Nadu and Tripura, it took sixteen or more months to incorporate the information in the
Central Registers. The Committee is aware that there is a provision in the IMCC Act 1970
mandating the State Boards to submit updated registers of practitioners on the 1st April
every year. The Committee would, therefore, like to be intimated of the impediment coming
in the way of updation of Central Registers of Indian Medicine and Homoeopathy despite
there being mandatory legal provisions. The matter may be taken up at the Minister level
and frequent review meetings be held.
IV. NATIONAL INSTITUTES
National Institute of Ayurveda (NIA)
4.1 The National Institute of Ayurveda was established on 7/2/1976 as an apex Institute of
Ayurveda in the country to develop high standards of teaching, training and research in all aspects
of Ayurvedic system of Medicine with a scientific approach.
4.2 In reply to a query, it has been informed that there are thirty five vacancies in Group ‘A’
posts. It has also been informed by the Department that 25 posts have been advertised, 7 posts
have fallen vacant recently for which necessary action is to be taken to fill up the posts and 3
posts are to be filled up by DPC shortly.
4.3 The Committee observes that the NIA is inter-alia mandated to develop high
standards of teaching in Ayurvedic System of Medicine and therefore the acute shortage of
the faculty is certain to adversely affect the functioning of this premier Institute. The
Committee, therefore, recommends that the Department should take immediate measures

10
towards filling up vacancies in faculty posts with priority and urgency. The Committee also
observes that in pursuance of the recommendation of the Committee, the Department in its
Action Taken Note on the 55
th Report of the Committee, had assured to take action to
appoint professionally qualified persons on short-term contract or deputation basis to
overcome the staff crunch in senior faculty positions. The Committee is not aware whether
any forward movement has been made in this regard. The Committee, therefore,
recommends to the Department to take immediate action towards appointing professionally
qualified persons on short-term contract or deputation against these posts till regular
appointments are made and desires to be kept apprised of the headway made in the matter.
National Institute of Homoeopathy (NIH)
4.4 The National Institute of Homoeopathy (NIH) was established in 1975 as a model Institute
in Homoeopathy. The main objective of the Institute is to develop excellence in Homoeopathic
education and conduct UG and PG courses.
4.5 On being asked about the updated status of expansion of NIH, the Department has inter alia
informed that the administrative approval and expenditure sanction has been obtained for the
construction of Academic-cum-Library Building Phase – II and III and the cost of the Project is
Rs.19.72 crore. It has also been informed that the project is expected to be completed by 2015
and the executing agency is M/s. NPCCL.
4.6 The Committee observes that the delay in completion of projects often results in cost
overrun. The Committee would, therefore, like the Department to closely monitor the
progress of construction of Academic-cum-Library Building on a quarterly basis in order to
avoid time overrun and resultant cost escalation.
4.7 In reply to another query, the Department has informed that the original cost of
Construction of Hospital Extension Building was Rs.11.59 crore, but M/s CPWD, the executing
agency, has revised the cost to Rs.13.08 crore. It has been further informed that 90% of civil
works has been completed.
4.8 The Committee observes that the expansion of the Hospital from 100 to 250 beds was
targeted to be achieved during 2010-11. Two years have elapsed since then, but the project
is yet to completed. The time-overrun has led to cost overrun. The Committee has been
advising the Department to streamline its monitoring mechanism so that such slippages in
timely implementing the project and the resultant cost overrun could be minimized. The
Committee is constrained to observe that the delay in completion of the project is indicative
of slack monitoring and bad planning. The Committee, therefore, exhorts the Department
to pay focused attention towards expansion of the Hospital from its existsing bed strength
of 100 to 250 beds. The Committee desires to be kept apprised of the progress of
implementation of the project.
4.9 On being asked about the updated status of vacancies at NIH, the Department has inter alia
informed that out of 75 sanctioned Group A posts, there are 31 vacancies. It has also been stated
that a preliminary screening of applications in respect of 8 posts has been done and interview is
to be held for final selection. The vacancy notice for remaining post has been sent to DAVP for
advertisement.
4.10 The Committee expresses its concern over such a large number of vacant posts in
teaching cadre which is certain to impair the functioning of NIH. The Committee observes
that the main objective of NIH is to develop excellence in homoeopathic education and
conduct UG and PG courses. It is, therefore, imperative for the Department to urgently take
steps to fill up the vacancies in a specific time-frame. The Committee desires to be apprised

11
of the measures taken by the Department and progress made towards filling up all vacant
posts of NIH.

4.13 The Committee observes that one of the main factors contributing to underutilization

activities for the new schemes/additional components under the above head so that the

4.15 The Committee, welcomes the evaluation of the Advanced Centres of Yoga by the

North Eastern Institute of Ayurveda and Homoeopathy (NEIAH), Shillong
4.16 The Union Cabinet in its meeting held on 27
th March, 2008 accorded approval for
establishment of North Eastern Institute of Ayurveda and Homoeopathy at Shillong to provide health
care to the people of NE Region and Sikkim under Ayurveda and Homoeopathy systems of
medicine. The Institute is to have Ayurvedic and Homoeopathic colleges with the admission
capacity of 50 students each along with a 100 bed Ayurvedic Hospital and a 50 bed Homoeopathic
Hospital comprising Documentation-cum-R&D Centre and Pharmacy with Drug Testing Laboratory.
4.17 As per the information furnished, the total outlay for NEIAH in the Twelfth Plan is
Rs.146.51 crore and the same will be utilized to set up the Institute by completing construction
of building, purchase of equipments and furniture, hospital activity and starting academic session.
Shedding light on the updated status of operationalization of the Institute, the Department has
informed that construction of buildings including Hospital Block, Teaching Block, Library Block,
Administration Block is in progress. The project is being monitored by a Project Management
Committee headed by the Secretary (AYUSH). The revised timeline for completion of civil work
of the project is October, 2013.
4.18 The Committee notes that the proposal for establishment of NEIAH was approved by
the Cabinet on the 27
th March, 2008. More than five years have passed since then, but the
full operationalisation of the project is still a far cry. Though the Department claims that
there is no cost escalation so far, the Committee is convinced that the delay is certain to
entail cost overruns. The Committee gathers from the information furnished that out of
Rs.64.50 crore allocated during the Eleventh Plan, Rs.45.00 crore only could be utilized which

12
is indicative of the inefficient utilization of the budgeted funds. The Committee, therefore,
desires that an action plan be drawn for better deployment of the financial resources during
the Twelfth Plan so that any possibility of financial under-performance could be obviated and
there is no breach of the revised time-line of October, 2013 for the operationalization of
NEIAH.
North Eastern Institute of Folk Medicine (NEIFM), Passighat, Arunachal Pradesh
4.19 The North Eastern Institute of Folk Medicine (NEIFM) is a National Institute under the
Department of AYUSH. It is being developed as a Centre of Excellence and apex research centre
for all aspects of Folk Medicine knowledge with linkages and collaborations with other research
institutions. The aims and objectives of the NEIFM are to survey, document and validate folk
medicine practices, remedies and therapies prevalent in the North East Region, with a view to
revitalize, promote and harness local health traditions and flora. The Cabinet had accorded approval
to establishment of the NEIFM on 21
st February, 2008.
4.20 The Eleventh Plan outlay for NEIFM was Rs. 41.00 crore, the allocation for BE (2007 to
2012) was Rs. 27.69 crore and for RE (2007 to 2012) Rs. 21.29 crore against which the actual
expenditure incurred during the Eleventh Plan was Rs.10.60 crore. As per the information
furnished by the Department, outlay for NEIFM for Twelfth Plan is Rs. 72.90 crore. The original
time-line for execution of the project was January, 2010 which could not be adhered to due to
various constraints including delay in transfer of 40 acres of land by the State Government.
Subsequently, the project was rescheduled to be completed by June, 2011. The Department
has now informed that the revised time-line for completion of civil work of the project is
October, 2013. It has also been informed that the original cost of the project was Rs. 32.88 crore
and that till now, there is no proposal for escalation of cost estimate.
4.21 The Committee is constrained to note the contradictions in the information furnished
by the Department. On the one hand, the Department claims that there is no proposal for
escalation of the cost estimate of the project, on the other, the approved outlay of Rs. 72.90
crore for the project gives an impression that the enhanced allocation has been made to
meet the cost overrun. The Committee, therefore, like the Department to explain this
apparent contradiction.
4.22 The Committee is also not happy with the tardy progress made towards
operationalisation of the project. A delay of more than three years have already taken
place, which is inordinate by any standard. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the
Department streamline its monitoring mechanism and ensure that the revised time-line for
completion of the project is not extended in any event. The Committee desires to be
apprised of the steps taken to ensure timely implementation of this project.
4.23 In reply to a query regarding the status of creation of posts for NEIFM, the Department
has informed that a proposal for creation of 159 posts has been received from NEIFM, which is
being examined in consultation with Internal Finance Division for processing further to obtain
approval of the Department of Expenditure.
4.24 The Committee observes that this project is intended to validate folk medicine
practices and integrate them into mainstream health care system. However, its
operationalisation in the true sense of the word can not be accomplished until the requisite
faculty and staff are appointed. The Committee, therefore, recommends to the Department
to proactively process the matter in the Integrated Finance Division and thereafter pursue
it with the Department of Expenditure. The Committee desires to be kept apprised of the
progress made in this regard.

13

VIII. QUALITY CONTROL OF AYURVEDA, SIDDHA, UNANI AND HOMOEOPATHIC
(ASU&H) DRUGS
8.1 The AYUSH system of medicine is governed by Drug and Cosmetics Act, 1940 and Rules
1945. Enforcement provisions of Chapter IV A of the Act is responsibility of State Governments.
Establishment of State Drug Testing Laboratories is also a statutory responsibility of States under
the Act. To provide financial assistance to States for strengthening enforcement mechanism, the
Drug Quality Control was started in the Eleventh Plan.
8.2 As per the information given in the Outcome Budget 2013-14, standardization of quality
control of ASU&H drugs as per the global trends is the prime concern of the Department of AYUSH.
8.3 In reply to a question, the Department has submitted that the following steps have been
taken to strengthen the regulatory mechanisms of ASU&H drugs:–
“(A) In order to improve the regulatory and Quality Control situation of ASU&H drugs in
the country, the Department of AYSUH set up Pharmacopoeia Commission of Indian
Medicine in 2010 to oversee the development of pharmacopoeial standards of drugs
and implemented a Centrally Sponsored Scheme since Ninth Plan to strengthen the
infrastructure and functional capacity of Drug Testing Laboratories and Pharmacies
and enforcement mechanism in the States. 29 State Drug Testing Laboratories, 46
State Pharmacies and 30 State Licensing Authorities have been supported through the
Centrally Sponsored Scheme and subsidy provided to private drug manufacturing
units for improving in-house Quality Control Laboratories as per GMP requirements.
(B) Besides, following regulatory measures under Drugs and Cosmetics Rules, 1945 have
been taken and Executive Orders issued to step up quality control of ASU&H drugs:–
(i) Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) for ASU&H drugs notified followed by
GMP supplementary guidelines for manufacturing of Mineral and Herbo-mineral
formulations.
(ii) Standards to be complied in the manufacture of ASU&H drugs notified.
(iii) Regulatory provision for recognition of laboratories for testing ASU drugs and
raw materials has been made under the Drugs and Cosmetics Rules. Joint
inspection by the representatives of Central Government and State Licensing
Authorities initiated for recognition of Drug Testing Laboratories under the
Drugs and Cosmetics Rules.
(iv) Qualifications of the State Licensing Authorities for ASU drugs notified.
(v) Standard requirement of space and scientific manpower was prescribed for
approval to be granted for carrying out testing of ASU drugs.
(vi) To improve the shelf life and quality of ASU drugs, use of excipients was
permitted in their manufacture with specific conditions and permissible limits.
(vii) Quality and safety assurance of drugs has been promoted by prescribing
permissible limits of heavy metals, aflatoxins, pesticide residue and microbial
load and issue of orders for providing reports of batch to batch testing in the
public sector procurement of ASU medicines.
(viii) Pharmacopoeial Laboratory for Indian Medicine and Homoeopathic
Pharmacopoiea Laboratory have been notified as appellate laboratories for the
purpose of testing of ASU&H drugs.

19
(ix) Development of pharmacopoeial standards of complex multiingredient ASU
formulations has been given high priority.
(x) Ban imposed on the misleading use of prefix and suffix with the names of
classical ASU medicines and the draft Rules notified.
(xi) V oluntary quality certification scheme for AYUSH products started in
collaboration with Quality Council of India.
(xii) Shelf life/date of expiry for ASU medicines was notified under Drugs and
Cosmetics Rule 161 (B) for public safety.
(xiii) Guidelines for issue of manufacturing license to various types of Patent and
Proprietary ASU drugs notified to provide clarity about the requirement of
documents in support of efficacy and safety of ASU drugs.
(xiv) Six technical officers of the Department of AYUSH have been appointed under
Drugs and Cosmetics Rules 160 E and 160 F for discharging duties of
inspection of institutions carrying out testing of ASU drugs.
(xv) Drugs and Cosmetics Rule 161 pertaining to labeling provisions has been
amended for mandatory mention of botanical names and parts of plants used
in the Ayurveda, Siddha and Unani formulations.
(xvi) Actions have been initiated on the recommendations of Ayurveda Siddha Unani
Drugs Technical Advisory Board (ASUDTAB) for regulating retail sale of ASU
drugs containing toxic raw material, development of Good Clinical Practice
Guidelines for clinical trials on ASU drugs and development of model laboratory
practices for testing of ASU drugs.
8.4 The roadmap for strengthening the quality control of ASU&H drugs in Twefth Plan aims
at enhancing the domain and scope of the Centrally Sponsored Scheme with addition of more
components and revision of funding pattern and establishment of a separate Central Drug Controller
for AYUSH.”
8.5 The Committee takes note of the steps taken by the Department for strengthening
of the regulatory mechanism of ASU&H drugs. However, the Committee is aware that
quality control and standardization of ASU&H drugs, which are mainly herbal/herbo-mineral
preparations, is very complex and different from synthetic molecules of the allopathic
system which are produced under controlled laboratory conditions. However, given the
current scenario where regulation of ASU&H drugs leaves much to be desired, the
Committee feels that strengthening and streamlining of regulatory mechanism of ASU&H
drugs needs to be speeded up. The Committee desires that the Department should accord
high priority to the task of laying down standards of quality control of ASU&H drugs by
using modern techniques.
8.6 The Department has informed that an outlay of Rs. 80.00 crore has been approved in the
Twelfth Plan for the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Quality Control of ASU&H drugs. It is
intended to revise the scheme based on its evaluation report and suggestions from stakeholders and
add new components. The given allocation is envisaged to be spent for focused outcomes in terms
of effective quality control of ASU&H drugs including strengthening of regulatory infrastructure,
mechanism and capacity in the States; improving drug manufacturing, storage and testing facilities
in public sector; implementation of regulatory capacity building initiatives; and development of
regulatory and quality control materials.

20
8.7 In reply to a question, the Department has informed that One State Drug Testing
Laboratory (DLT) and one State Ayurvedic Pharmacy have been assisted with grant-in-aid of
Rs.21.31 lakhs and Rs.43.46 lakhs respectively. Two GMP compliant private drugs manufacturing
units availed subsidy in 2012-13. The proposals of three more State DTLs and one Pharmacy
for balance grant-in-aid have been approved by the Project Screening Committee and are in
pipeline for release of funds. With the available funds and existing funding pattern of the scheme,
it is intended to support 5 DTLs, 5 Pharmacies, 5 Licensing Authorities and 6 manufacturing
units in 2013-14. However, revision of the scheme with inclusion of new components may revise
these targets.
8.8 The Committee observes that there is a separate chapter-IV A in the Drugs and
Cosmetics Act 1940 which regulates the manufacture and sale of ASU drugs. Since the
enforcement of provisions of Drugs and Cosmetics Act and Rules made thereunder is under
the purview of State Drug Licensing and Drug Control Authorities, the State drugs
regulatory framework has a crucial role to play in ensuring safety and quality of ASU&H
drugs. It is in this context that strengthening of State Drug Testing Laboratories which are
facing infrastructure constraints, and shortage of manpower, assumes added significance.
The Committee, therefore, recommends to the Department to quickly revise the Quality
Control Scheme and its funding pattern for greater efficacy of the Scheme.
Central Drug Controller for AYUSH
8.9 The Committee has been informed that a Central Regulatory Authority for ASU&H drugs is
contemplated to be set up. The Department in a written submission has informed that the matter
of establishing Central Drug Controller for AYUSH has been constantly pursued with the
Department of Expenditure for creation of posts. Certain specific clarifications and justification for
the required posts have been provided in February, 2013. Allocation of Rs. 102 crore in Twelfth
Plan and Rs. 7.60 crore in the annual plan 2013-14 has been budgeted to undertake the
establishment of infrastructure and manpower for the Central AYUSH Drug Controller’s office.
Proposal is also being moved for acquiring additional space to accommodate the AYUSH Drug
Controller’s office.
8.10 On being asked as to why it is not desirable to let CDSCO regulate ASU drugs also, the
Department has informed that CDSCO has been basically dealing with quality control of allopathic
drugs and accordingly, the whole paraphernalia there does not have the wherewithal to effectively
regulate ASU&H drugs. The basic reason is that ASU&H drugs are distinct from allopathic drugs
in terms of philosophy, principles, concepts, standards, quality aspects, applications, numbers and
count of manufacturing units and testing requirements and they need to have different regulations.
In-spite of common Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940, the regulatory issues of ASU&H drugs are
not being taken care of by the Central Drugs Controller Office due to non-availability of requisite
expertise and huge workload of matters related to allopathic drugs. The idea of having a common
Central Drugs Authority with Additional Drug Controller of AYUSH had not been earlier agreed to.
However, the office of the Drug Controller General (India) was strengthened by sanctioning 175
posts for modern medicine and was renamed as Central Drugs Standards Control Organisation
(CDSCO), but no posts were sanctioned for the Indian Systems of Medicine and Homoeopathy.
It was thereafter only that in accordance with the recommendations of a high powered Committee
and ASU Drugs Consultative Committee and considering the specific regulatory requirements of
ASU&H drugs, setting up a separate Central Drugs Controller of AYUSH was found to be a
necessary requirement.
8.11 An early action may be taken to establish and appoint AYUSH Drug Controller.

information:–
“As recommended by the Hon’ble Parliamentary Committee, the matter of checking
objectionable advertisements on AYUSH drugs has been taken up with Ministry of
Information & Broadcasting and Directorate of Audio-visual Publicity (DAVP) with a
request to take action as appropriate for stopping improper advertisements on AYUSH in
electronic and print media. DA VP has informed that it does not have regulatory power
over private advertisement. Press Council of India has also informed that as per the Press
Council Act, 1978 the Council enjoys statutory authority for the print media and it is
sensitive on the issue of objectionable advertisements and have norms of Journalistic
Conduct-2010. However, these guidelines carry only ethical backing as there are no
enforcement powers with the Press Council of India. The matter is being pursued with
Ministry of Information and Broadcasting. The Department of AYUSH has also written to
all State Drug Licensing Authorities/Drug Controllers of AYUSH to bring instances of
misleading advertisements concerning AYUSH drugs in TV, Radio and print media to the
notice of Ministry of Information and Broadcasting for remedial action and to take
corrective measures in preventing inappropriate advertisements in electronic and print
media including newspapers.”
11.7 The Committee observes that no tangible progress has been made towards curtailing
misleading advertisements concerning AYUSH, over the electronic media and in the print
media. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Department should pursue the
matter with the authorities concerned with renewed vigour as the issue is too important for
maintaining credibility of AYUSH systems to be left unattended. The Committee desires to
be apprised of the final outcome in the matter.
XII. MISCELLANEOUS
12.1 The Committee observes that 20 yoga therapy Centres were targeted to be set up in
AYUSH/Allopathy hospitals during the Eleventh Plan, but only 6 such centres could be set
up during the Plan period. The Committee expresses its displeasure over this sorry state of
affairs and strongly recommends that such yoga therapy centres be set in all AYUSH/

24
Allopathy hospitals all over the country during the current Plan period. The Committee
would like to be apprised of the progress made in this regard.
12.2 The Committee also observes that during the Eleventh Plan, 150 tours for
documentation of reported cases of prevention/ treatment of vector-borne/infectious diseases
by Siddha Drugs were targeted; however, only 31 tours could be conducted. The Committee
is of the view that there is an urgent need for improvement in documentation of the
reported episodes of prevention/ treatment of vector-borne/infectious diseases by Siddha
drugs and recommends that the Department should make all out efforts to complete
documentation of all the reported cases of prevention/ treatment/cure of vector-borne/
infectious diseases not only by Siddha drugs but also by Ayurvedic and other traditional
drugs.

OBSERV ATIONS/RECOMMENDATIONS — AT A GLANCE
II. BUDGETARY ALLOCATION
The Committee is concerned to note that except for the year 2010-11, the total actual
expenditure has invariably been considerably lower than Budget Estimates, particularly in
2011-12 and 2012-13. For Example, the total actual expenditure for the year 2008-09 was
Rs. 471.13 crore against Budget Estimates (BE) of Rs. 534.00 crore; for the year 2009-10,
Rs. 678.97 crore as against BE of Rs. 734.00 crore; for the year 2011-12, Rs. 611.46 crore
as against BE of 900.00 crore; and for the year 2012-13, Rs. 580.27 crore as against BE of
Rs. 990.00 crore. The Committee is not happy with this recurrent and persistent under
utilization of plan funds allocated for the Department. The Committee is constrained to
observe that such a persistent shortfall in the utilization of plan funds is indicative of fiscal
indiscipline and serious shortcoming in formulating the Budget Estimates. The Committee
in its 55
th Report on Demands for Grants (2012-13) of the Department had recommended to
take measures for exercising greater fiscal prudence. However, underutilization of the funds
to the tune of Rs. 409.73 crore vis-a-vis  BE for 2012-13 indicates that the Committee’s
advice was not heeded to. The Committee, therefore, even at the cost of repetition, strongly
recommends that concrete measures be taken to exercise utmost fiscal discipline and
ensure absorption of the allocated funds. (Para 2.5)
The Committee notes that the extent of surrendered funds is substantially higher
under Centrally Sponsored Schemes (30.9% with reference to RE) than that under Central
Sector Schemes (7.8% with reference to RE). The Committee also takes note of the
remedial steps for better absorption of funds but is not impressed by the half measures
taken by the Department to overcome the sub-optimal utilization of Plan funds as it is
obvious that these efforts have not yielded the desired results. In view of the fact that the
allocations have persistently remained under-utilized in the past several years, the
Department should have undertaken a comprehensive analysis in this regard and taken
corrective measures accordingly. Now that an evaluation of all the Schemes is being done
by an independent agency, the Committee is sanguine that the corrective measures will be
initiated for ensuring optimal and judicious utilization of the budgeted funds. The
Committee recommends that the evaluation be completed in a time-bound manner. The
Committee desires to be apprised of the outcome of the independent evaluation and action
taken thereon. The Committee would also like the Department to devise ways to evaluate
the impact of its various schemes. The Committee, simultaneously, impresses upon the
Department to be more prudent in their budget formulation and project their fund
requirements in a more realistic manner after timely collection of all the information
pertaining to fund requirements from the State Governments. (Para 2.6)
The Committee notes that a provision of Rs. 1069.00 crore has been made in B.E
2013-14 on the plan side. The Committee would expect the Department to initiate concrete
measures at least from this year onwards to ensure that the sanctioned funds are
administered in a more diligent manner. The Committee desires to be kept apprised of the
steps taken for more efficient deployment and utilization of the funds budgeted for 2013-14.
(Para 2.7)
The Committee also takes note of the fact that the share of AYUSH in the total
health outlay has been substantially enhanced to Rs. 10044.00 crore in the Twelfth Plan,
30

31
which is an increase of 235.47% over the actual expenditure of Eleventh Plan of Rs. 2994.00
crore. The Committee is aware that health needs of a vast and diverse country like India
cannot be met by a single healthcare system and AYUSH health care systems have a very
vital role to play in expanding the outreach of health care to the people because of their
inherent advantages in terms of diversity, modest cost, low level of technological input, etc.
Indian system of medicines and  traditional medicines should be complementary to Modern
system of Medicine. It is in this context that the Committee welcomes the enhanced
allocation of funds for AYUSH in the Twelfth Plan. The Committee also appreciates the
efforts made by the Department in getting enhanced allocation for the year 2013-14 inspite
of the fact that there was considerable underutilization of funds during the previous year
i.e. 2012-13. Persistent underutilization of funds to such extent is a serious concern for the
Committee. The Committee is also apprehensive about the utilization of such enhanced
allocation in 2013-14. Therefore, the Committee would expect the Department to put in
place a dedicated mechanism for stricter expenditure monitoring and financial discipline so
that the scarce resources do not remain locked up and surrendered later. (Para 2.8)
Pending Utilization Certificates
The Committee observes that pendency of UCs and the huge amount involved therein
have implications for further release of funds and thus impinges on the effective
implementation of the projects. Though the Department has drawn up an ambitious plan of
reducing pendency of UCs to nil, the past trends in this regard inspire little confidence. The
Committee, therefore, desires to be informed of the detailed action plan on bringing down
the pendency of UCs to nil and the success achieved so far so that a fair assessment could
be made about the efficacy of the plan. (Para 2.10)
It is a matter of serious concern for the Committee to note that the number of
pending UCs and the amount involved therein is too substantial to be ignored. Of more
serious concern is the fact that UCs dating as far back as to 2000 and 2001 are still
pending. The Committee notes with disapproval that the steps taken by the Department for
liquidation of the pending UCs are of routine nature and have not yielded the desired
results so far. The Committee would, therefore, like the Department to expedite evaluation
of the schemes and formulate appropriate remedial measures accordingly. The Committee
would also expect the Department to play a more proactive role in the capacity building of
the States so that with better absorption capacity the funds could be utilized in a more
efficient manner. The Committee would also like to reiterate its recommendation made in
its 55
th Report presented to Rajya Sabha on 26 th April, 2012 that the Department should
formulate an action plan in coordination with the State Governments for developing an
effective and efficient coordination mechanism for timely submission of UCs. This would
also speed up execution of all the projects well within the approved cost. (Para 2.13)
Utilization of Plan Allocation for North-Eastern States and Sikkim
The Committee lends its full support to the activities and budgetary provisions for
the benefit of the North-Eastern States and Sikkim. The Committee observes that it is
essential for inclusive growth that the benefits of the growth of our economy reach the
people of the distantly located North-Eastern States of the country. The Committee would,
therefore, like the Department to closely monitor the progress of various schemes in the
North-Eastern Region and ensure that the ongoing projects there are not hamstrung for
lack of funds or due to underutilization thereof. The Committee would also like to impress
upon the Department to ensure that the projects/schemes sanctioned for the North-Eastern
Region are not delayed due to lack of approvals. (Para 2.18)

32
III. Updation of Central Registers of Indian Medicine and Homoeopathy
The Committee is not happy to note that despite its recommendation made in its 55 th
Report on Demands for Grants (2012-13) of the Department that all such information
should be made available in the public domain in an updated form on the touch of a button,
little progress seems to have been made in this regard, which is evident from the fact that
out of 23 States in respect of which information pertaining to updation of Central Register
of Indian Medicine has been made available, eight States are lagging behind in sending
updated information. As regards the Status of updation of the Central Register of
Homoeopathy, the Committee is surprised to note that in three cases, i.e. Bihar, Tamil
Nadu and Tripura, it took sixteen or more months to incorporate the information in the
Central Registers. The Committee is aware that there is a provision in the IMCC Act 1970
mandating the State Boards to submit updated registers of practitioners on the 1
st April
every year. The Committee would, therefore, like to be intimated of the impediment coming
in the way of updation of Central Registers of Indian Medicine and Homoeopathy despite
there being mandatory legal provisions. The matter may be taken up at the Minister level
and frequent review meetings be held. (Para 3.2)
IV. National Institutes
National Institute of Ayurveda (NlA)
The Committee observes that the NIA is inter-alia mandated to develop high
standards of teaching in Ayurvedic System of Medicine and therefore the acute shortage of
the faculty is certain to adversely affect the functioning of this premier Institute. The
Committee, therefore, recommends that the Department should take immediate measures
towards filling up vacancies in faculty posts with priority and urgency. The Committee also
observes that in pursuance of the recommendation of the Committee, the Department in its
Action Taken Note on the 55
th Report of the Committee, had assured to take action to
appoint professionally qualified persons on short-term contract or deputation basis to
overcome the staff crunch in senior faculty positions. The Committee is not aware whether
any forward movement has been made in this regard. The Committee, therefore,
recommends to the Department to take immediate action towards appointing professionally
qualified persons on short-term contract or deputation against these posts till regular
appointments are made and desires to be kept apprised of the headway made in the matter.
(Para 4.3)
National Institute of Homoeopathy (NIH)
The Committee observes that the delay in completion of projects often results in cost
overrun. The Committee would, therefore, like the Department to closely monitor the
progress of construction of Academic-cum-Library Building on a quarterly basis in order to
avoid time overrun and resultant cost escalation. (Para 4.6)
The Committee observes that the expansion of the Hospital from 100 to 250 beds was
targeted to be achieved during 2010-11. Two years have elapsed since then, but the project
is yet to completed. The time-overrun has led to cost overrun. The Committee has been
advising the Department to streamline its monitoring mechanism so that such slippages in
timely implementing the project and the resultant cost overrun could be minimized. The
Committee is constrained to observe that the delay in completion of the project is indicative
of slack monitoring and bad planning. The Committee, therefore, exhorts the Department
to pay focused attention towards expansion of the Hospital from its existsing bed strength

33
of 100 to 250 beds. The Committee desires to be kept apprised of the progress of
implementation of the project. (Para 4.8)
The Committee expresses its concern over such a large number of vacant posts in
teaching cadre which is certain to impair the functioning of NIH. The Committee observes
that the main objective of NIH is to develop excellence in homoeopathic education and
conduct UG and PG courses. It is, therefore, imperative for the Department to urgently take
steps to fill up the vacancies in a specific time-frame. The Committee desires to be apprised
of the measures taken by the Department and progress made towards filling up all vacant
posts of NIH. (Para 4.10)
Morarji Desai National Institute of YOGA (MDNIY)
The Committee observes that one of the main factors contributing to underutilization
of the budgeted funds is delay in necessary approvals. The Committee would, therefore, like
to impress upon the Department to proactively pursue and complete all pre-approval
activities for the new schemes/additional components under the above head so that the
approved outlay for the Twelfth Plan is utilized gainfully and there are no instances of sub-
optimal utilization of the approved outlay. (Para 4.13)
The Committee, welcomes the evaluation of the Advanced Centres of Yoga by the
Scientific Advisory Committee and desires to be apprised of its findings and action taken
thereon. (Para 4.15)
North Eastern Institute of Ayurveda and Homeopathy (NEIAH), Shillong
The Committee notes that the proposal for establishment of NEIAH was approved by
the Cabinet on the 27
th March, 2008. More than five years have passed since then, but the
full operationalisation of the project is still a far cry. Though the Department claims that
there is no cost escalation so far, the Committee is convinced that the delay is certain to
entail cost overruns. The Committee gathers from the information furnished that out of
Rs. 64.50 crore allocated during the Eleventh Plan, Rs. 45.00 crore only could be utilized
which is indicative of the inefficient utilization of the budgeted funds. The Committee,
therefore, desires that an action plan be drawn for better deployment of the financial
resources during the Twelfth Plan so that any possibility of financial under-performance
could be obviated and there is no breach of the revised time-line of October, 2013 for the
operationalization of NEIAH. (Para 4.18)
North-Eastern Institute for Folk Medicine (NEIFM), Pasighat, Arunachal Pradesh
The Committee is constrained to note the contradictions in the information furnished
by the Department. On the one hand, the Department claims that there is no proposal for
escalation of the cost estimate of the project, on the other, the approved outlay of Rs. 72.90
crore for the project gives an impression that the enhanced allocation has been made to
meet the cost overrun. The Committee, therefore, like the Department to explain this
apparent contradiction. (Para 4.21)
The Committee is also not happy with the tardy progress made towards
operationalisation of the project. A delay of more than three years have already taken
place, which is inordinate by any standard. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the
Department streamline its monitoring mechanism and ensure that the revised time-line for
completion of the project is not extended in any event. The Committee desires to be
apprised of the steps taken to ensure timely implementation of this project. (Para 4.22)

34
The Committee observes that this project is intended to validate folk medicine
practices and integrate them into mainstream health care system. However, its
operationalisation in the true sense of the word can not be accomplished until the requisite
faculty and staff are appointed. The Committee, therefore, recommends to the Department
to proactively process the matter in the Integrated Finance Division and thereafter pursue
it with the Department of Expenditure. The Committee desires to be kept apprised of the
progress made in this regard. (Para 4.24)
All India Institute of Ayurveda (AIIA), New Delhi
In its 55
th Report presented to Rajya Sabha on 26 th April, 2012, the Committee had

The Committee is constrained to note that despite the Department’s assurance made in past

V . Centrally Sponsored Scheme for Development of AYUSH Institutions
The Committee does not understand as to why State Governments do not come
forward to get funds for strengthening the AYUSH colleges. The Department should make
an introspection in this regard and discuss with State Governments. (Para 5.4)
The Committee would recommend to the Department to expedite submission of the
report of the independent agency and find out the exact reasons for gross underutilization
of the budgeted amount under the above head and take corrective action accordingly by way
of making realistic projection of budgetary requirements and optimal utilization thereof.
The Committee would also like to be apprised of the findings of the independent agency and
action taken thereon. (Para 5.5)
The Committee observes that a substantial outlay of Rs. 450.00 crore has been
approved for the above scheme for the Twelfth Plan. The Committee would like the
Department to gear up its monitoring mechanism so as to avoid recurrence of such gross
financial underperformance as witnessed duing the Eleventh Plan. (Para 5.6)
VI. Assistance to Accredited AYUSH Centres of Excellence in Non-Governmental/Private
Sector Engaged in AYUSH Education/Drug Development
The Committee is constrained to observe that this is yet another instance of
unrealistic formulation of Budget Estimate and under utilization thereof. The Committee
disapproves of such unrealistic projection of fund requirements and impresses upon the
Department to ensure that such large variations in the Budget Estimates, Revised Estimates
and Actual Expenditure do not recur in future. (Para 6.6)
The Committee gathers from the information furnished that the Scheme is being
evaluated by an independent agency and would be modified as per its suggestions. The
Committee welcomes this exercise and desires to be apprised of the follow-up action taken
in this regard. (Para 6.7)
The Committee would also like to draw attention of the Department to the fact that
on the one hand, the Department has informed that the outlay for the Scheme for the

35
Twelfth Plan is Rs. 97.50 crore, on the other, the Outcome Budget 2013-14 States that the
Scheme was only for the Eleventh Plan and fresh proposal could be considered only on
approval of continuation of this Scheme. The Committee would, therefore, like the
Department to justify as to how such a huge amount of Rs. 97.50 crore is targeted to be
utilized if the continuation of the above Scheme is yet to be approved, though the first year
of the Twelfth Plan has already elapsed. When the experience in the Eleventh Plan shows
that there are very few eligible non-profit NGOs/Private Sector organizations in AYUSH,

VII. Research and Development including Medicinal Plants
The Committee notes that the outlay for the above head for the Twelfth Plan is
substantially higher than the Eleventh Plan allocations. A large number of important
activities are included under this head. The Committee is of the view that scientific
validation of classical formulations of Indian Systems of Medicine for their safety and
efficacy is of vital importance for promotion of these systems of medicine. The Committee,
therefore, desires that the Department should regularly monitor the utilization of allocated
funds under this head to ensure that the funds are utilized judiciously and the on-going
research activities are strengthened. (Para 7.2)
The Committee would also like to reiterate its recommendation made in its 55
th
Report presented to Rajya Sabha on 26 th April, 2012 that the Department should establish
a national registry of all AYUSH research studies and get the health outcomes accruing
from the research projects of the Research Councils evaluated by an independent agency.
The Committee desires to be apprised of the developments in this regard. (Para 7.3)
National Medicinal Plants Board (NMPB)
The Committee is of the view that full-fledged SMPBs with full-time chief Executive

fledged SMPBs. (Para 7.8)
The Committee notes with concern that a substantial amount of Central funds for
the previous years continues to remain unaccounted for under both the schemes of NMPB
which is indicative of non-adherence to the basic financial norms. The Committee feels that
the delay in timely submission of UCs would adversely affect execution of the projects under
this head. The Committee would, therefore, recommend the Department to draw up a
concrete action plan for quicker liquidation of pending UCs within a designated time-line.
The Committee desires to be kept apprised of the measures taken and results achieved in
this regard. (Para 7.9)
The Committee has also been given to understand that an evaluation of the Schemes
of NMPB is going on and in the light of the suggestions made, the NMPB will be revised.

of the suggestions made and action taken thereon. (Para 7.10)
The Committee notes that in pursuance of its recommendation, some progress has
been made towards filling up of the posts. The Committee would like to impress upon the
Department to vigorously pursue the matter and ensure that the remaining vacancies are
